bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第111卷 卷第一百一十一 。

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 111, Volume the One Hundred and Eleventh.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 111.

sentences.zh: 【】 ◎晉紀三十三起屠維大淵獻，盡上章困敦，凡二年。。

translations.literal: 【】 ◎ Jin Records 33: beginning from Tuyi Dayuanxian, ending at Shangzhang Kundun—in all, two years.
translations.idiomatic: 【Jin Records 33】 From the year Tuyi Dayuanxian through Shangzhang Kundun—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 安皇帝丙隆安三年（己亥，公元三九九年） 。

translations.literal: Emperor An, year 3 of Longan (jihai, AD 399).
translations.idiomatic: Year 3 of Longan under Emperor An of Jin (jihai, AD 399).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛酉，大赦。。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day xinyou, there was a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on xinyou day, the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，燕昌黎尹留忠謀反，誅，事連尚書令東陽公根、尚書段成，皆坐死；

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, Liu Zhong, governor of Changli under Yan, plotted rebellion and was executed; the affair implicated the Director of the Masters of Writing, the Duke of Dongyang Gen, and the Master of Writing Duan Cheng—both were put to death for their connection;
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day, Liu Zhong, the Yan governor of Changli, was executed for plotting rebellion. The case implicated Gen, Duke of Dongyang and Director of the Masters of Writing, and Duan Cheng, a Master of Writing—both were put to death as accomplices.

sentences.zh: 遣中衛將軍衛雙就誅忠弟幽州刺史志於凡城。

translations.literal: The court dispatched the Central Guard General Wei Shuang to execute Zhong's younger brother Zhi, the Inspector of Youzhou, at Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Central Guard General Wei Shuang to Fancheng to execute Zhong's younger brother Zhi, who was Inspector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 以衛將軍平原公元為司徒、尚書令。。

translations.literal: The Guardian General, the Duke of Pingyuan Yuan, was appointed Grand Minister over the Masses and Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, Duke of Pingyuan and Guardian General, was appointed Grand Minister over the Masses and Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 庚午，魏主珪北巡，分命大將軍常山王遵等三軍東道出長川，鎮北將軍高涼王樂真等七軍從西道出牛川，珪自將大軍從中道出駮髯水以襲高車。。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, the Wei ruler Gui made a northern tour. He divided his forces and ordered the Grand General, the Prince of Changshan Zun, and two other armies to march east by way of Changchuan; the Pacifier of the North, the Prince of Gaoliang Lezhen, and six other armies to march west by way of Niuchuan; Gui himself led the main army on the central route through the Bojian River to strike the Gaoche.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day, the Wei ruler Tuoba Gui toured the north. He sent three armies east along Changchuan under Grand General Prince Changshan Zun; seven armies west through Niuchuan under Pacifier of the North Prince Gaoliang Lezhen; and led the main force himself on a central route along the Bojian River to attack the Gaoche.

sentences.zh: 壬午，燕右將軍張真、城門校尉和翰坐謀反誅。。

translations.literal: On the day renwu, Zhang Zhen, Right General of Yan, and He Han, Colonel of the City Gates, were executed for plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day, Zhang Zhen, Right General of Yan, and He Han, Colonel of the City Gates, were executed for treason.

sentences.zh: 癸未，燕大赦，改元長樂。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei, Yan proclaimed a great amnesty and changed the reign title to Changle.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day, Yan granted a general amnesty and adopted the reign title Changle.

sentences.zh: 燕主盛每十日一自決獄，不加拷掠，多得其情。。

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Sheng personally judged cases every ten days, without applying torture, and in most cases obtained the true facts.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan ruler Murong Sheng personally heard cases every ten days, forbore torture, and in most instances arrived at the truth.

sentences.zh: 武威王烏孤徙治樂都，以其弟西平公利鹿孤鎮安夷，廣武公辱檀鎮西平，叔父素渥鎮湟河，若留鎮澆河，從弟替引鎮嶺南，洛回鎮廉川，從叔吐若留鎮浩亹；

translations.literal: The Prince of Wuwei, Wugu, moved his capital to Ledu. He stationed his younger brother, the Duke of Xiping Lilugu, at Anyi; the Duke of Guangwu Rutan at Xiping; his uncle Suwo at Huanghe; Ruoliu at Jiaohe; his younger cousin Tiyin at Lingnan; Luohui at Lianchuan; and his uncle Turuoliu at Hao'ai;
translations.idiomatic: Wugu, Prince of Wuwei, moved his seat to Ledu. He posted his younger brother Lilugu, Duke of Xiping, at Anyi; Rutan, Duke of Guangwu, at Xiping; his uncle Suwo on the Huang River; Ruoliu on the Jiao River; his cousin Tiyin in Lingnan; Luohui in Lianchuan; and his uncle Turuoliu at Hao'ai;

sentences.zh: 夷、夏俊傑，隨才授任，內居顯位，外典郡縣，鹹得其宜。。

translations.literal: Talented men, both barbarian and Chinese, were appointed according to their abilities—some holding high office at court, others governing commanderies and districts—and all were suitably placed.
translations.idiomatic: Able men from both the tribal and Chinese populations were assigned posts according to talent—some to high office at court, others to govern counties and commanderies—and all were well matched to their roles.

sentences.zh: 烏孤謂群臣曰：「隴右、河西，本數郡之地，遭亂分裂至十餘國，呂氏、乞伏氏、段氏最強。

translations.literal: Wugu said to his ministers: "Longyou and Hexi were originally the territory of several commanderies, but through disorder they split into more than ten states. The Lü clan, the Qifu clan, and the Duan clan are the strongest.
translations.idiomatic: Wugu told his ministers, "Longyou and Hexi were once a few commanderies, but turmoil has split them into more than a dozen states. The Lü, Qifu, and Duan clans are the strongest.

sentences.zh: 今欲取之，三者何先？」

translations.literal: Now that we wish to take them, which of the three should we strike first?"
translations.idiomatic: If we mean to seize them, which should we attack first?"

sentences.zh: 楊統曰：「乞伏氏本吾之部落，終當服從。

translations.literal: Yang Tong said: "The Qifu clan were originally our tribe; in the end they will submit.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tong replied, "The Qifu were once our own tribe—they will submit in time.

sentences.zh: 段氏書生，無能為患，且結好於我，攻之不義。

translations.literal: The Duan clan are mere scholars and cannot become a threat; moreover they are on friendly terms with us, and to attack them would be unjust.
translations.idiomatic: The Duan are bookish men who pose no real danger, and they are already friendly with us—an attack would be unjust.

sentences.zh: 呂光衰耄，嗣子微弱，纂、弘雖有才而內相猜忌，若使浩亹、廉川乘虛迭出，彼必疲於奔命，不過二年，兵勞民困，則姑臧可圖也。

translations.literal: Lü Guang is old and feeble, his heir weak. Although Zuan and Hong are talented, they are mutually suspicious within. If we send forces from Hao'ai and Lianchuan to strike in succession when they are exposed, the enemy will be worn out running to meet us. Within two years at most, with troops exhausted and the people distressed, Guzang can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang is senile and his heir feeble. Zuan and Hong may be capable, but they distrust each other. If we launch repeated raids from Hao'ai and Lianchuan while their defenses are thin, they will wear themselves out rushing to respond. In no more than two years, with their armies exhausted and their people strained, Guzang will be within our grasp.

sentences.zh: 姑臧舉，則二寇不待攻而服矣。」

translations.literal: Once Guzang is taken, the other two foes will submit without our needing to attack them."
translations.idiomatic: Once Guzang falls, the other two rivals will yield without a fight."

sentences.zh: 烏孤曰：「善。」。

translations.literal: Wugu said: "Excellent."
translations.idiomatic: Wugu said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 二月，丁亥朔，魏軍大破高車二十餘部，獲七萬餘口，馬三十餘萬匹，牛羊百四十餘萬頭。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the first day dinghai, the Wei army routed more than twenty Gaoche tribes, capturing over seventy thousand persons, more than three hundred thousand horses, and more than 1.4 million head of cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on dinghai, the first day of the month, the Wei army crushed more than twenty Gaoche tribes, taking over seventy thousand captives, more than three hundred thousand horses, and over 1.4 million head of cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 衛王儀別將三萬騎絕漠千餘里，破其七部，獲二萬餘口，馬五萬餘匹，牛羊二萬餘頭。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wei, Yi, with a separate command of thirty thousand horsemen, crossed more than a thousand li of desert and broke seven tribes, taking more than twenty thousand persons, more than fifty thousand horses, and more than twenty thousand head of cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei Yi led thirty thousand horsemen on a separate route more than a thousand li across the desert, defeated seven tribes, and captured over twenty thousand people, fifty thousand horses, and twenty thousand cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 高車諸部大震。。

translations.literal: All the Gaoche tribes were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoche tribes were thrown into great alarm.

sentences.zh: 林邑王范達陷日南、九真，遂寇交趾，太守杜瑗擊破之。。

translations.literal: Fan Da, king of Linyi, seized Rinan and Jiuzhen and then raided Jiaozhi; the prefect Du Yuan defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Da, king of Linyi, captured Rinan and Jiuzhen and then invaded Jiaozhi, but Prefect Du Yuan routed his forces.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，魏徵虜將軍庾岳破張超於勃海，斬之。。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, Yu Yue, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians of Wei, defeated Zhang Chao at Bohai and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day, Yu Yue, Wei's General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, defeated Zhang Chao at Bohai and executed him.

sentences.zh: 段業即涼王位，改元天璽。

translations.literal: Duan Ye assumed the throne of Liang and changed the reign title to Tianxi.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye took the throne of Liang and proclaimed the reign title Tianxi.

sentences.zh: 以沮渠蒙遜為尚書左丞，梁中庸為右丞。。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun was appointed Left Director of the Masters of Writing, and Liang Zhongyong Right Director.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun was made Left Director of the Masters of Writing and Liang Zhongyong Right Director.

sentences.zh: 魏主珪大獵於牛川之南，以高車人為圍，周七百餘里；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler Gui held a great hunt south of Niuchuan, using Gaoche men to form the beaters in an enclosure more than seven hundred li in circumference;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler Gui held a great hunt south of Niuchuan, using Gaoche tribesmen to form a seven-hundred-li drive;

sentences.zh: 因驅其禽獸，南抵平城，使高車築鹿苑，廣數十里。

translations.literal: he then drove the game south as far as Pingcheng and had the Gaoche build a deer park several tens of li across.
translations.idiomatic: then drove the game south to Pingcheng and set the Gaoche to building a deer park several tens of li wide.

sentences.zh: 三月，己未，珪還平城。。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day jiwei, Gui returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiwei day, Gui returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 甲子，珪分尚書三十六曹及外署，凡置三百六十曹，令八部大夫主之。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, Gui divided the thirty-six bureaus of the Masters of Writing and the outer offices, establishing in all three hundred sixty bureaus, each to be headed by one of the eight great chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day, Gui reorganized the thirty-six bureaus of the Masters of Writing and the outer offices into three hundred sixty bureaus, each placed under one of the eight great chieftains.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書崔宏通署三十六曹，如令、僕統事。

translations.literal: Cui Hong, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, supervised all thirty-six bureaus, like a chief minister directing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hong, Minister of Personnel, oversaw all thirty-six bureaus in the manner of a chief minister coordinating the administration.

sentences.zh: 置五經博士，增國子太學生員合三千人。。

translations.literal: Five Erudites for the Five Classics were appointed, and the enrollment of the Imperial University was increased to three thousand students in all.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Erudites for the Five Classics and raised enrollment at the Imperial University to three thousand students.

sentences.zh: 珪問博士李先曰：「天下何物最善，可以益人神智？」

translations.literal: Gui asked the Erudite Li Xian: "What thing under Heaven is best able to improve a man's spirit and understanding?"
translations.idiomatic: Gui asked Erudite Li Xian, "What in the world best sharpens the mind and spirit?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「莫若書籍。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Nothing surpasses books."
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian answered, "Nothing surpasses books.

sentences.zh: 珪曰：「書籍凡有幾何，如何可集？」

translations.literal: Gui said: "How many books are there in all, and how can they be gathered?"
translations.idiomatic: Gui asked, "How many books exist, and how could we collect them all?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「自書契以來，世有滋益，以至於今，不可勝計。

translations.literal: He replied: "Since the invention of writing, each age has added to their number down to the present, and they are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian replied, "Since writing began, each generation has added to the store until today—they are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 苟人主所好，何憂不集！」

translations.literal: If the ruler desires them, what worry is there that they cannot be assembled!"
translations.idiomatic: But if the sovereign wills it, what is there to fear—they will be gathered."

sentences.zh: 珪從之，命郡縣大索書籍，悉送平城。。

translations.literal: Gui followed this advice and ordered the commanderies and districts to search widely for books and send them all to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Gui took his advice and ordered every commandery and district to scour for books and send them to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 初，秦王登之弟廣帥眾三千依南燕王德，德以為冠軍將軍，處之乞活堡。

translations.literal: Earlier, Guang, younger brother of Fu Deng, king of Qin, had led three thousand men to attach himself to Murong De, king of Southern Yan. De made him Champion General and quartered him at Qihuo Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Fu Guang, younger brother of Former Qin ruler Fu Deng, had brought three thousand followers to serve Murong De of Southern Yan, who made him Champion General and stationed him at Qihuo Fort.

sentences.zh: 會熒惑守東井，或言秦當復興，廣乃自稱為秦王，擊南燕北地王鐘，破之。

translations.literal: When Mars occupied the Well constellation, some said that Qin was due to rise again. Guang thereupon styled himself King of Qin, attacked Zhong, the Prince of Northern Yan, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Mars stood in the Well mansion, some said Former Qin would rise again. Guang proclaimed himself King of Qin, attacked Murong Zhong, Prince of Northern Yan, and routed him.

sentences.zh: 是時，滑台孤弱，土無十城，眾不過一萬，鐘既敗，附德者多去德而附廣。

translations.literal: At this time Huatai was isolated and weak, with fewer than ten walled places and a force of no more than ten thousand. Once Zhong was defeated, many who had adhered to De left De and went over to Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Huatai was then isolated and weak—fewer than ten walled towns and barely ten thousand men. After Zhong's defeat, many of De's adherents deserted him for Guang.

sentences.zh: 德乃留魯陽王和守滑台，自帥眾討廣，斬之。。

translations.literal: De thereupon left Murong He, Prince of Luyang, to guard Huatai and personally led his troops to campaign against Guang and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: De left Prince Luyang He to hold Huatai and marched in person against Guang, whom he killed.

sentences.zh: 燕主寶之至黎陽也，魯陽王和長史李辨勸和納之，和不從。

translations.literal: When the Yan ruler Bao reached Liyang, Murong He, Prince of Luyang, and his chief clerk Li Bian urged He to welcome him in; He would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Bao of Yan reached Liyang, Prince Luyang He and his chief clerk Li Bian urged He to receive him; He refused.

sentences.zh: 辨懼，故潛引晉軍至管城，欲因德出戰而作亂。

translations.literal: Bian was afraid and therefore secretly brought Jin troops to Guancheng, intending to raise a revolt when De marched out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for himself, Bian secretly guided Jin troops to Guancheng, planning to rebel while De was away campaigning.

sentences.zh: 既而德不出，辨愈不自安。

translations.literal: When De did not go out, Bian became still more uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: When De never marched out, Bian grew only more anxious.

sentences.zh: 及德討苻廣，辨復勸和反。

translations.literal: When De campaigned against Fu Guang, Bian again urged He to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When De set out against Fu Guang, Bian again pressed He to rebel.

sentences.zh: 和不從，辨乃殺和，以滑台降魏。

translations.literal: He would not agree, so Bian killed He and surrendered Huatai to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He again refused, so Bian killed him and surrendered Huatai to Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏行台尚書和跋在鄴，帥輕騎自鄴赴之。

translations.literal: He Ba, Director of the Masters of Writing on the Wei field staff, was at Ye; he led light cavalry from Ye to go to him.
translations.idiomatic: He Ba, Director of the Masters of Writing on Wei's field staff at Ye, rode with light cavalry from Ye to take possession.

sentences.zh: 既至，辨悔之，閉門拒守。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Bian repented and shut the gates to resist.
translations.idiomatic: When He Ba arrived, Bian regretted his decision and shut the gates to resist.

sentences.zh: 跋使尚書郎鄧暉說之，辨乃開門內跋，跋悉收德宮人府庫。

translations.literal: Ba sent the Master of Writing Attendant Deng Hui to persuade him; Bian then opened the gates and admitted Ba, who seized all of De's palace women and the treasury stores.
translations.idiomatic: Ba sent Master of Writing Attendant Deng Hui to negotiate; Bian opened the gates and admitted him. He Ba then seized De's palace women and treasury.

sentences.zh: 德遣兵擊跋，跋逆擊，破之，又破德將桂陽王鎮，俘獲千餘人。

translations.literal: De sent troops to strike Ba; Ba met them in counterattack and defeated them, and also defeated De's general Murong Zhen, Prince of Guiyang, capturing more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: De sent troops against He Ba, who met them in counterattack and routed them, then defeated De's general Prince Guiyang Zhen and took more than a thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 陳、穎之民多附於魏。。

translations.literal: Many of the people of Chen and Ying went over to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Many people in Chen and Ying districts went over to Wei.

sentences.zh: 南燕右衛將軍慕容雲斬李辨，帥將士家屬二萬餘口出滑台赴德。

translations.literal: Murong Yun, Right Guard General of Southern Yan, beheaded Li Bian and led more than twenty thousand soldiers and their families out of Huatai to join De.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yun, Southern Yan's Right Guard General, killed Li Bian and led more than twenty thousand soldiers and dependents out of Huatai to rejoin De.

sentences.zh: 德欲攻滑台，韓范曰；

translations.literal: De wished to attack Huatai. Han Fan said:
translations.idiomatic: De wanted to retake Huatai. Han Fan said,

sentences.zh: 「向也魏為客，吾為主人；

translations.literal: "Formerly Wei was the guest and we were the host;
translations.idiomatic: "Before, Wei was the guest and we the host;

sentences.zh: 今也吾為客，魏為主人。

translations.literal: now we are the guest and Wei is the host.
translations.idiomatic: now we are the guest and Wei the host.

sentences.zh: 人心危懼，不可復戰，不如先據一方，自立基本，乃圖進取。」

translations.literal: Men's hearts are fearful and alarmed; we cannot fight again. It would be better first to secure a territory of our own, establish a base, and only then plan advance."
translations.idiomatic: Our men are frightened and in no state to fight again. We should secure a territory, build a foundation, and only then plan our next move."

sentences.zh: 張華曰：「彭城，楚之舊都，可攻而據之。」

translations.literal: Zhang Hua said: "Pengcheng is the old capital of Chu; we can attack and hold it."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua said, "Pengcheng is the ancient capital of Chu—we can seize and hold it.

sentences.zh: 北地王鐘等皆勸德攻滑台。

translations.literal: Murong Zhong, Prince of Northern Yan, and others all urged De to attack Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Northern Yan Zhong and others all urged De to retake Huatai.

sentences.zh: 尚書潘聰曰：「滑台四通八達之地，北有魏，南有晉，西有秦，居之未嘗一日安也。

translations.literal: Pan Cong, Master of Writing, said: "Huatai is a place where roads run in every direction. Wei lies to the north, Jin to the south, and Qin to the west; whoever holds it has not had a single day of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Pan Cong said, "Huatai sits at a crossroads—Wei to the north, Jin to the south, Qin to the west. No one who holds it has known a day of peace.

sentences.zh: 彭城土曠人稀，平夷無險，且晉之舊鎮，未易可取。

translations.literal: Pengcheng has broad lands and a sparse population; the terrain is level and open without natural defenses, and as an old Jin garrison it will not be easy to take.
translations.idiomatic: Pengcheng is broad and thinly peopled, flat and without natural defenses—and as a former Jin stronghold, it will not be easy to take.

sentences.zh: 又密邇江、淮，夏秋多水。

translations.literal: It also lies close to the Yangzi and Huai rivers, which run high in summer and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: It also lies close to the Yangzi and Huai, which flood in summer and autumn.

sentences.zh: 乘舟而戰者，吳之所長，我之所短也。

translations.literal: Fighting from boats is what Wu excels at and what we do poorly.
translations.idiomatic: River warfare is Wu's strength and our weakness.

sentences.zh: 青州沃野二千里，精兵十餘萬，左有負海之饒，右有山河之固，廣固城曹嶷所築，地形阻峻，足為帝王之都。

translations.literal: Qingzhou has two thousand li of fertile fields and more than a hundred thousand picked troops. To the left lies the wealth of the sea coast; to the right, the security of mountains and rivers. The city of Guanggu, built by Cao Yi, has steep and defensible terrain and is fully fit to serve as an imperial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou offers two thousand li of rich land and more than a hundred thousand seasoned troops. To the east lies the wealth of the coast; to the west, mountain barriers. Guanggu, built by Cao Yi, is steep and defensible—fit for an imperial capital.

sentences.zh: 三齊英傑，思得明主以立功於世久矣。

translations.literal: The outstanding men of the Three Qi have long wished for a wise ruler through whom they might win merit in the world.
translations.idiomatic: The able men of the Three Qi have long yearned for a worthy ruler under whom they could win glory.

sentences.zh: 辟閭渾昔為燕臣，今宜遣辨士馳說於前，大兵繼踵於後，若其不服，取之如拾芥耳。

translations.literal: Pilü Hun was once a Yan subject; now we should send eloquent envoys ahead to persuade him while a great army follows close behind. If he will not submit, taking the land will be like picking up a mustard leaf.
translations.idiomatic: Pilü Hun once served Yan. Send eloquent envoys ahead and follow with a great army. If he refuses, taking his territory will be as easy as picking up a mustard seed.

sentences.zh: 既得其地，然後閉關養銳，伺隙而動，此乃陛下之關中、河內也。」

translations.literal: Once we have secured that territory, we can then shut the passes, rest our sharp edge, and move when an opening appears—this will be Your Majesty's Guanzhong and Henei."
translations.idiomatic: Once we hold that land, shut the passes, rest our forces, and strike when opportunity appears—that will be Your Majesty's Guanzhong and Henei."

sentences.zh: 德猶豫未決。

translations.literal: De hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: De remained undecided.

sentences.zh: 沙門竺朗素善占候，德使牙門蘇撫問之，朗曰：「敬覽三策，潘尚書之議，興邦之言也。

translations.literal: The monk Zhu Lang was skilled in divination and astrology. De sent the gate officer Su Fu to question him. Lang said: "I have respectfully reviewed the three plans. Master of Writing Pan's proposal is language that would raise a state.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Zhu Lang was skilled in divination. De sent gate officer Su Fu to consult him. Zhu Lang said, "I have weighed all three plans. Master of Writing Pan's is the counsel that would found a kingdom.

sentences.zh: 且今歲之初，彗星起奎、婁，掃虛、危；

translations.literal: Moreover, at the beginning of this year a comet rose in Kui and Lou and swept through Xu and Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, early this year a comet rose in Kui and Lou and swept through Xu and Wei.

sentences.zh: 彗者，除舊布新之象，奎、婁為魯，虛、危為齊。

translations.literal: a comet is the sign of removing the old and laying out the new. Kui and Lou correspond to Lu; Xu and Wei to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: A comet means clearing away the old to make way for the new. Kui and Lou signify Lu; Xu and Wei signify Qi.

sentences.zh: 宜先取兗州，巡撫琅邪，至秋乃北徇齊地，此天道也。」

translations.literal: We should first take Yanzhou, pacify Langye, and only in autumn march north to overrun the land of Qi—this is Heaven's way."
translations.idiomatic: You should first take Yanzhou and secure Langye, then in autumn march north into Qi—this is Heaven's course."

sentences.zh: 撫又密問以年世，朗以《周易》筮之曰：「燕衰庚戌，年則一紀，世則及子。」

translations.literal: Fu also asked secretly about the span of years. Lang divined with the Book of Changes and said: "Yan will decline in gengxu; the term of years will be one cycle, and the succession will reach the son."
translations.idiomatic: Su Fu also asked privately about the dynasty's span. Zhu Lang divined with the Book of Changes and said, "Yan will decline in the year gengxu—twelve years in all, and the succession will reach the son's generation.

sentences.zh: 撫還報德，德乃引師而南，兗州北鄙諸郡縣皆降之。

translations.literal: Fu returned and reported to De, whereupon De led his army south; all the commanderies and districts on the northern border of Yanzhou submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Su Fu reported back, and De marched south. Every commandery and district on the northern fringe of Yanzhou submitted.

sentences.zh: 德置守宰以撫之，禁軍士無得虜掠。

translations.literal: De appointed guards and magistrates to pacify them and forbade the soldiers to plunder or seize captives.
translations.idiomatic: De appointed officials to govern them and forbade his soldiers from looting.

sentences.zh: 百姓大悅，牛酒屬路。。

translations.literal: The common people were greatly pleased; cattle and wine lined the roads.
translations.idiomatic: The people rejoiced, and the roads were lined with offerings of cattle and wine.

sentences.zh: 丙子，魏主珪遣建義將軍庾真、越騎校尉奚斤擊庫狄、宥連、侯莫陳三部，皆破之，追奔至大峨谷，置戍而還。。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, the Wei ruler Gui dispatched the General Who Establishes Righteousness Yu Zhen and the Colonel of Agile Cavalry Xi Jin to attack the three tribes Kudi, Youlian, and Houmochen. All were defeated; the pursuit ran to the Great E Valley, where garrisons were set and the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day, Tuoba Gui sent General Who Establishes Righteousness Yu Zhen and Colonel of Agile Cavalry Xi Jin against the Kudi, Youlian, and Houmochen tribes. All were defeated; the pursuit reached Great E Valley, where garrisons were posted before the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 己卯，追尊帝所生母陳夫人為德皇太后。。

translations.literal: On the day jimao, the Emperor's biological mother, Lady Chen, was posthumously honored as the Virtuous Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day, the emperor's birth mother, Lady Chen, was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager De.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，鮮卑疊掘河內帥戶五千降於西秦。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, five thousand households under Dieju, a Xianbei leader in Henei, surrendered to Western Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, five thousand households under the Xianbei leader Dieju of Henei surrendered to Western Qin.

sentences.zh: 西秦王乾歸以河內為疊掘都統，以宗女妻之。。

translations.literal: The Western Qin king Gangui appointed Dieju chief commander in Henei and gave him a clan daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Western Qin ruler Qifu Gangui appointed Dieju chief commander in Henei and gave him a clan daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 甲午，燕大赦。。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, Yan proclaimed a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day, Yan proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 會稽王道子有疾，且無日不醉。

translations.literal: The Prince of Kuaiji, Daozi, was ill and not a day passed without his being drunk.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Kuaiji, Sima Daozi, was ill and drank himself drunk every day without fail.

sentences.zh: 世子元顯知朝望去之，乃諷朝廷解道子司徒、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: The heir Yuanxian, knowing the court looked down on his father, thereupon prompted the court to relieve Daozi of his posts as Minister over the Masses and Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The heir Sima Yuanxian, knowing the court despised his father, prompted the court to strip Daozi of the posts of Minister over the Masses and Inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以元顯為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, Yuanxian was made Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day, Yuanxian was appointed Inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 道子醒而後知之，大怒，無如之何。

translations.literal: Daozi learned of it only after sobering up, was greatly angry, and could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi learned of it only after he sobered up. He was furious but could do nothing.

sentences.zh: 元顯以廬江太守會稽張法順為謀主，多引樹親黨，朝貴皆畏事之。。

translations.literal: Yuanxian took Zhang Fashun of Kuaiji, Administrator of Lujiang, as his chief strategist, brought in and cultivated many relatives and partisans, and all the court nobles feared and served him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian made Zhang Fashun of Kuaiji, Administrator of Lujiang, his chief strategist, brought in many relatives and allies, and all the great officials at court feared and deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 燕散騎常侍餘超、左將軍高和等坐謀反誅。。

translations.literal: Yu Chao, Palace Attendant of Yan, Left General Gao He, and others were executed for plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chao, Palace Attendant of Yan, Left General Gao He, and others were executed for plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 涼太子紹、太原公纂將兵伐北涼，北涼王業求救於武威王烏孤，烏孤遣驃騎大將軍利鹿孤及楊軌救之。

translations.literal: The Liang crown prince Shao and the Prince of Taiyuan, Zuan, led troops to attack Northern Liang. The Northern Liang king Ye sought rescue from Tufa Wugu, Prince of Wuwei; Wugu sent Flying Cavalry General Lilugu and Yang Gui to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang crown prince Shao and Prince of Taiyuan Zuan led troops against Northern Liang. Northern Liang ruler Duan Ye sought help from Tufa Wugu, Prince of Wuwei, who sent Flying Cavalry General Lilugu and Yang Gui to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 業將戰，沮渠蒙遜諫曰：「楊軌恃鮮卑之強，有窺窬之志，紹、纂深入，置兵死地，不可敵也。

translations.literal: Ye was about to give battle. Juqu Mengxun remonstrated, saying: "Yang Gui relies on Xianbei strength and harbors designs of encroachment. Shao and Zuan have penetrated deep and placed their troops in a death trap—they cannot be opposed.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was about to fight when Juqu Mengxun remonstrated: "Yang Gui relies on Xianbei strength and harbors aggressive designs. Shao and Zuan have marched deep and put their army in a death trap—we cannot stand against them.

sentences.zh: 今不戰則有泰山之安，戰則有累卵之危。」

translations.literal: If we do not fight now, we have the security of Mount Tai; if we fight, we have the peril of a pile of eggs."
translations.idiomatic: If we do not fight, we have the security of Mount Tai; if we fight, we face peril as fragile as a pile of eggs."

sentences.zh: 業從之，案兵不戰。

translations.literal: Ye followed this advice and held his troops without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Ye took his advice and held his army back without giving battle.

sentences.zh: 紹、纂引兵歸。。

translations.literal: Shao and Zuan withdrew their troops and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shao and Zuan withdrew their armies.

sentences.zh: 六月，烏孤以利鹿孤為涼州牧，鎮西平，召車騎大將軍辱檀入錄府國事。。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Wugu made Lilugu Governor of Liangzhou, stationed at Xiping, and summoned Chariots and Cavalry General Rutan to enter the capital and manage state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Wugu made Lilugu Governor of Liangzhou and stationed him at Xiping, then summoned Chariots and Cavalry General Rutan to the capital to manage state affairs.

sentences.zh: 會稽世子元顯自以少年，不欲頓居重任；

translations.literal: The Kuaiji heir Yuanxian, considering himself young, did not wish to remain long in a weighty post;
translations.idiomatic: The Kuaiji heir Yuanxian, considering himself too young, did not wish to remain long in so heavy a post;

sentences.zh: 戊子，以琅邪王德文為司徒。。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, the Prince of Langya, Dewen, was made Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day, Prince Langya Dewen was appointed Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 魏前河間太守范陽盧溥帥其部曲數千家，就食漁陽，遂據有數郡。

translations.literal: Lu Pu of Fanyang, former Administrator of Henei under Wei, led several thousand households of his following to seek food at Yuyang and thereupon seized control of several commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Pu of Fanyang, former Administrator of Henei under Wei, led several thousand households of his followers to Yuyang for provisions and then seized several commanderies.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己未，燕主盛遣使拜溥幽州刺史。。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day jiwei, the Yan ruler Sheng sent envoys to appoint Pu Governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on jiwei day, Yan ruler Murong Sheng sent envoys to appoint Lu Pu Governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，燕主盛下詔曰：「法例律，公侯有罪，得以金帛贖，此不足以懲惡而利於王府，甚無謂也。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, the Yan ruler Sheng issued an edict, saying: "In the statutes and precedents of law, when dukes and marquises were guilty they could redeem themselves with gold and silk. This is insufficient to punish evil and only benefits the royal treasury—it is quite pointless.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day, Murong Sheng issued an edict: "Under the statutes, dukes and marquises guilty of crimes could redeem themselves with gold and silk. That is not enough to punish wrongdoing and only enriches the royal treasury—it is utterly pointless.

sentences.zh: 自今皆令立功以自贖。

translations.literal: From now on all are ordered to redeem themselves by earning merit.
translations.idiomatic: From now on all must earn merit to redeem their offenses.

sentences.zh: 勿復輸金帛。。

translations.literal: Do not again pay gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: No more payments in gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 西秦丞相南川宣公出連乞都卒。。

translations.literal: Chilian Qidu, Duke of Chuannan Xuan, Chancellor of Western Qin, died.
translations.idiomatic: Chilian Qidu, Duke of Chuannan Xuan and Chancellor of Western Qin, died.

sentences.zh: 秦齊公崇、鎮東將軍楊佛嵩寇洛陽，河南太守隴西辛恭靖嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Chong, Duke of Qi of Qin, and Yang Fosong, General Who Pacifies the East, raided Luoyang; Xin Gongjing of Longxi, Administrator of Henan, closed the city and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin Duke of Qi Chong and General Who Pacifies the East Yang Fosong attacked Luoyang. Xin Gongjing of Longxi, Administrator of Henan, shut the city gates and held out.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史楊佺期遣使求救於魏常山王遵，魏主珪以散騎侍郎西河張濟為遵從事中郎以報之。

translations.literal: Yang Xianqi, Inspector of Yong Province, sent envoys seeking rescue from Tuoba Zun, Prince of Changshan of Wei; the Wei ruler Gui made Zhang Ji of Xihe, Palace Attendant, Attendant Master of Writing under Zun to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou Inspector Yang Xianqi sent envoys to seek help from Tuoba Zun, Prince of Changshan. Wei ruler Tuoba Gui sent Palace Attendant Zhang Ji of Xihe as Attendant Master of Writing under Zun to reply.

sentences.zh: 佺期問於濟曰：「魏之伐中山，戎士幾何？」

translations.literal: Xianqi asked Ji, saying: "When Wei attacked Zhongshan, how many warriors were there?"
translations.idiomatic: Xianqi asked Ji: "When Wei attacked Zhongshan, how many fighting men did you have?

sentences.zh: 濟曰：「四十餘萬」。

translations.literal: Ji said: "More than four hundred thousand."
translations.idiomatic: Ji replied: "More than four hundred thousand."

sentences.zh: 佺期曰：「以魏之強，小羌不足滅也。

translations.literal: Xianqi said: "With Wei's strength, the petty Qiang are not enough to destroy.
translations.idiomatic: Xianqi said: "With Wei's might, these petty Qiang are nothing you cannot crush.

sentences.zh: 且晉之與魏，本為一家，今既結好，義無所隱。

translations.literal: Moreover Jin and Wei were originally one family; now that we have made alliance, there is no reason to conceal anything.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and Wei were originally one house, and now that we are allied there is no reason to hide anything.

sentences.zh: 此間兵弱糧寡，洛陽之救，恃魏而已。

translations.literal: Our forces here are weak and supplies few; rescue for Luoyang depends entirely on Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Our army here is weak and supplies are scarce. Luoyang's rescue depends entirely on Wei.

sentences.zh: 若其保全，必有厚報；

translations.literal: If it is preserved, there will surely be rich reward;
translations.idiomatic: If the city is saved, you will surely receive rich reward;

sentences.zh: 若其不守，與其使羌得之，不若使魏得之。」

translations.literal: if it cannot be held, rather than let the Qiang get it, better to let Wei get it."
translations.idiomatic: if it cannot be held, better that Wei take it than that the Qiang do.

sentences.zh: 濟還報。

translations.literal: Ji returned and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Ji returned and reported this.

sentences.zh: 八月，珪遣太尉穆崇將六萬騎往救之。。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Gui sent Grand Commandant Mu Chong with sixty thousand horsemen to go rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Tuoba Gui sent Grand Commandant Mu Chong with sixty thousand horsemen to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 燕遼西太守李朗在郡十年，威行境內，恐燕主盛疑之，累征不赴。

translations.literal: Li Lang, Administrator of Liaoxi under Yan, had been in the commandery ten years; his authority ran throughout the territory. Fearing the Yan ruler Sheng would suspect him, he was repeatedly summoned but did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lang, Administrator of Liaoxi under Yan, had governed the commandery for ten years and his authority ran throughout it. Fearing Murong Sheng would suspect him, he ignored repeated summons.

sentences.zh: 以其家在龍城，未敢顯叛，陰召魏兵，許以郡降魏；

translations.literal: Because his family was in Longcheng, he did not dare openly rebel; secretly he summoned Wei troops, promising to surrender the commandery to Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Because his family was in Longcheng he did not dare rebel openly, but secretly summoned Wei troops and promised to surrender the commandery;

sentences.zh: 遣使馳詣龍城，廣張寇勢。

translations.literal: he sent envoys hastening to Longcheng, greatly exaggerating the threat of invasion.
translations.idiomatic: he sent envoys racing to Longcheng with greatly exaggerated reports of enemy pressure.

sentences.zh: 盛曰：「此必詐也。」

translations.literal: Sheng said: "This must be deception."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said: "This must be a ruse.

sentences.zh: 召使者詰問，果無事實。

translations.literal: He summoned the envoys and interrogated them; indeed there was no factual basis.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the envoys and questioned them closely, and there proved to be no truth in it.

sentences.zh: 盛盡滅朗族，丁酉，遣輔國將軍李旱討之。。

translations.literal: Sheng exterminated Lang's entire clan. On the day dingyou, he dispatched Li Han, General Who Supports the State, to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng exterminated Lang's entire clan. On dingyou day he sent General Who Supports the State Li Han to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 初，魏奮武將軍張袞以才謀為魏主珪所信重，委以腹心。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Gun, General Who Bestirs Martial Might of Wei, for his talent and stratagems was trusted and valued by the Wei ruler Gui, who entrusted him with his innermost counsels.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhang Gun, General Who Bestirs Martial Might, had been trusted and valued by Tuoba Gui for his talent and counsel, and was treated as a confidant.

sentences.zh: 珪問中州士人於袞，袞薦盧溥及崔逞，珪皆用之。。

translations.literal: Gui asked Gun about Central Plains gentlemen; Gun recommended Lu Pu and Cui Cheng, and Gui employed both.
translations.idiomatic: Gui asked Gun about men of the Central Plains. Gun recommended Lu Pu and Cui Cheng, and Gui employed them both.

sentences.zh: 珪圍中山，久未下，軍食乏，問計於群臣。

translations.literal: Gui besieged Zhongshan for a long time without taking it; army provisions were exhausted, and he asked his ministers for plans.
translations.idiomatic: Gui besieged Zhongshan for a long time without taking it. Army provisions ran short, and he asked his ministers for advice.

sentences.zh: 逞為御史中丞，對曰：「桑椹可以佐糧。

translations.literal: Cheng, as Censor-in-Chief, replied: "Mulberries can supplement grain.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Cheng, serving as Censor-in-Chief, replied: "Mulberries can supplement grain.

sentences.zh: 飛鴞食椹而改音，詩人所稱也。」

translations.literal: The flying crow eats mulberries and changes its cry—this is what the poets praise."
translations.idiomatic: The flying crow eats mulberries and changes its cry—that is what the poets praise.

sentences.zh: 珪雖用其言，聽民以椹當租，然以逞為侮慢，心銜之。

translations.literal: Though Gui followed this advice and allowed the people to pay rent in mulberries, he considered Cheng insolent and harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Gui took his advice and allowed the people to pay taxes in mulberries, but he considered Cheng insolent and nursed a grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 秦人寇襄陽，雍州刺史郗恢以書求救於魏常山王遵曰：「覽兄虎步中原。」

translations.literal: Qin forces raided Xiangyang. Xi Huai, Inspector of Yong Province, sent a letter seeking rescue from Tuoba Zun, Prince of Changshan of Wei, saying: "Your brother strides like a tiger across the Central Plains."
translations.idiomatic: Qin forces raided Xiangyang. Yongzhou Inspector Xi Huai sent a letter to Tuoba Zun, Prince of Changshan, seeking rescue: "Your brother marches like a tiger across the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 珪以恢無君臣之禮，命袞及逞為復書，必貶其主。

translations.literal: Gui, because Xi Huai lacked proper etiquette between ruler and subject, ordered Gun and Cheng to draft a reply that must demean his sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Gui considered Xi Huai's letter a breach of proper etiquette between ruler and subject and ordered Gun and Cheng to draft a reply that must demean the Jin emperor.

sentences.zh: 兗、逞謂帝為貴主，珪怒曰：「命汝貶之，而謂之『貴主』，何如『賢兄』也！」

translations.literal: Gun and Cheng called the emperor "honored sovereign"; Gui raged: "I ordered you to demean him, yet you call him 'honored sovereign'—how is that like calling him 'worthy elder brother'!"
translations.idiomatic: Gun and Cheng called the emperor "honored sovereign." Gui raged: "I ordered you to demean him, yet you call him 'honored sovereign'—how is that different from calling him 'worthy elder brother'!

sentences.zh: 逞之降魏也，以天下方亂，恐我復遺種，使其妻張氏與四子留冀州，逞獨與幼子賾詣平城，所留妻子遂奔南燕。

translations.literal: When Cheng had defected to Wei, because the realm was in turmoil he feared Wei would exterminate his seed; he left his wife Lady Zhang and four sons in Jizhou, and Cheng alone went with his youngest son Ze to Pingcheng. The wife and sons left behind then fled to Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Cheng had surrendered to Wei, fearing in the chaos that Wei might exterminate his line, he left his wife Lady Zhang and four sons in Jizhou and went alone with his youngest son Ze to Pingcheng. The family he left behind then fled to Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 珪並以是責逞，賜逞死。

translations.literal: Gui also blamed Cheng for this and ordered him to die.
translations.idiomatic: Gui also held this against Cheng and sentenced him to death.

sentences.zh: 盧溥受燕爵命，侵掠魏郡縣，殺魏幽州刺史封沓干。

translations.literal: Lu Pu accepted Yan's title and appointment, raided Wei commanderies and districts, and killed Feng Tagen, Inspector of Youzhou of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Pu accepted a title from Yan, raided Wei commanderies and districts, and killed Wei's Inspector of Youzhou Feng Tagen.

sentences.zh: 珪謂袞所舉皆非其人，黜袞為尚書令史。

translations.literal: Gui said everyone Gun had recommended was the wrong man and demoted Gun to Clerk of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Gui declared that none of Gun's recommendations had been suitable and demoted him to Clerk of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 袞乃闔門不通人事，惟手校經籍，歲餘而終。。

translations.literal: Gun then shut his gates to all human affairs, only personally collating the classics, and within a little more than a year died.
translations.idiomatic: Gun then shut his doors to the world, devoting himself only to collating the classics by hand, and died a little over a year later.

sentences.zh: 燕主寶之敗也，中書令、民部尚書封懿降於魏。

translations.literal: When the Yan ruler Bao was defeated, Feng Yi, Chief Secretary and Minister of the People, surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Bao of Yan was defeated, Chief Secretary and Minister of the People Feng Yi surrendered to Wei.

sentences.zh: 珪以懿為給事黃門侍郎、都坐大官。

translations.literal: Gui made Yi Palace Attendant in the Yellow Gate Office and Director of the Grand Commissary.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui made him Attendant in the Yellow Gate Office and Director of the Grand Commissary.

sentences.zh: 珪問懿以燕氏舊事，懿應對疏慢，亦坐廢於家。。

translations.literal: Gui questioned Yi about old Yan affairs; Yi's replies were careless and disrespectful, and he was also dismissed to live at home.
translations.idiomatic: Gui questioned him about old affairs of the Murong house. Feng Yi's answers were careless and disrespectful, and he too was dismissed to live at home.

sentences.zh: 武威王禿髮烏孤醉，走馬傷脅而卒，遺令立長君。

translations.literal: Tufa Wugu, Prince of Wuwei, while drunk rode a horse, injured his flank, and died; his testament ordered the eldest son to be established.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Wugu, Prince of Wuwei, while drunk rode a horse, injured his side, and died. His final orders were to establish the eldest son.

sentences.zh: 國人立其弟利鹿孤，謚烏孤曰武王，廟號列祖。

translations.literal: The people of the state established his younger brother Lilugu; Wugu's posthumous title was Wu Wang, and his temple name Liezu.
translations.idiomatic: The people established his younger brother Lilugu instead. Wugu was given the posthumous title Wu Wang and the temple name Liezu.

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤大赦，徙治西平。。

translations.literal: Lilugu proclaimed a great amnesty and moved the capital to Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu proclaimed a general amnesty and moved the capital to Xiping.

sentences.zh: 南燕王德遣使說幽州刺史辟閭渾，欲下之，渾不從。

translations.literal: Murong De, king of Southern Yan, sent envoys to persuade Pilü Hun, Inspector of Youzhou, to submit; Hun would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De of Southern Yan sent envoys to persuade Youzhou Inspector Pilü Hun to submit, but Hun refused.

sentences.zh: 德遣北地王鐘帥步騎二萬擊之，德進據琅邪，徐、兗之民歸附者十餘萬。

translations.literal: De sent Murong Zhong, Prince of Northern Yan, leading twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack him. De advanced and occupied Langya; more than one hundred thousand people of Xu and Yan provinces came to join him.
translations.idiomatic: De sent Prince of Northern Yan Murong Zhong with twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack him, then advanced and occupied Langya. More than one hundred thousand people of Xu and Yan provinces came over to him.

sentences.zh: 德自琅邪引兵而北，以南海王法為兗州刺史，鎮梁父。

translations.literal: De himself led troops north from Langya, made Murong Fa, Prince of Nanhai, Inspector of Yanzhou, and stationed him at Liangfu.
translations.idiomatic: De himself marched north from Langya, made Prince of Nanhai Murong Fa Inspector of Yanzhou, and stationed him at Liangfu.

sentences.zh: 進攻莒城，守將任安委城走。

translations.literal: He attacked Jucheng; the defending general Ren An abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Jucheng. The defending general Ren An abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 德以潘聰為徐州刺史，鎮莒城。

translations.literal: De made Pan Cong Inspector of Xuzhou and stationed him at Jucheng.
translations.idiomatic: De made Pan Cong Inspector of Xuzhou and stationed him at Jucheng.

sentences.zh: 蘭汗之亂，燕吏部尚書封孚南奔辟閭渾，渾表為勃海太守；

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Lan Han, Feng Fu, Minister of the Masters of Writing of Yan, fled south to Pilü Hun; Hun memorialized to make him Administrator of Bohai;
translations.idiomatic: During the turmoil of Lan Han, Yan Minister of the Masters of Writing Feng Fu fled south to Pilü Hun, who memorialized to make him Administrator of Bohai;

sentences.zh: 及德至，孚出降，德大喜曰：「孤得青州不為喜，喜得卿耳！」

translations.literal: When De arrived, Fu came out and surrendered. De said joyfully: "I am not happy to have gained Qingzhou—I am happy to have gained you!"
translations.idiomatic: When De arrived, Feng Fu came out and surrendered. De said joyfully: "I am not happy to have gained Qingzhou—I am happy to have gained you!

sentences.zh: 遂委以機密。

translations.literal: Thereupon he entrusted him with confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He then entrusted him with confidential state affairs.

sentences.zh: 北地王鐘傳檄青州諸郡，諭以禍福，辟閭渾徙八千餘家入守廣固，遣司馬崔誕戊薄荀固，平原太守張豁戌柳泉；

translations.literal: Murong Zhong, Prince of Northern Yan, issued proclamations to the commanderies of Qingzhou, explaining blessings and calamities. Pilü Hun moved more than eight thousand households into Guanggu to defend it, sent Sima Cui Yan to garrison Bo and Xun Gu, and Pingyuan Administrator Zhang Huo to garrison Liuquan;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Northern Yan Murong Zhong issued proclamations to the commanderies of Qingzhou, explaining the consequences of submission or resistance. Pilü Hun moved more than eight thousand households into Guanggu to defend it, sent Sima Cui Yan to garrison Bo and Xun Gu, and Pingyuan Administrator Zhang Huo to garrison Liuquan;

sentences.zh: 誕、豁承檄皆降於德。

translations.literal: Yan and Huo, upon receiving the proclamation, both surrendered to De.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yan and Zhang Huo both surrendered to De upon receiving the proclamation.

sentences.zh: 渾懼，攜妻子奔魏，德遣射聲校尉劉綱追之，及於莒城，斬之。

translations.literal: Hun was afraid, fled with wife and children to Wei. De sent Liu Gang, Commandant of the Archers, in pursuit; he caught up with him at Jucheng and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Hun was terrified and fled with his wife and children to Wei. De sent Commandant of the Archers Liu Gang in pursuit, caught up with him at Jucheng, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 渾子道秀自詣德，請與父俱死。

translations.literal: Hun's son Daoxiu came to De himself, asking to die together with his father.
translations.idiomatic: Hun's son Daoxiu came to De of his own accord and asked to die with his father.

sentences.zh: 德曰：「父雖不忠，而子能孝。」

translations.literal: De said: "Though the father was disloyal, the son can be filial."
translations.idiomatic: De said: "Though the father was disloyal, the son can be filial.

sentences.zh: 特赦之。

translations.literal: He specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He specially pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 渾參軍張瑛為渾作檄，辭多不遜，德執而讓之。

translations.literal: Zhang Ying, an aide of Hun, had drafted a proclamation for Hun with language mostly insolent; De seized him and rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Hun's aide Zhang Ying had drafted a proclamation for him in language mostly insolent. De seized him and rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 瑛神色自若，徐曰：「渾之有臣，猶韓信之有蒯通。

translations.literal: Ying's expression was calm as before; he said slowly: "Hun had his minister, just as Han Xin had Kuai Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's expression remained calm. He said slowly: "Hun had his minister, just as Han Xin had Kuai Tong.

sentences.zh: 通遇漢祖而生，臣遭陛下而死。

translations.literal: Kuai Tong met Han's founder and lived; I meet Your Majesty and die.
translations.idiomatic: Kuai Tong met the founder of Han and lived; I meet Your Majesty and die.

sentences.zh: 比之古人，竊為不幸耳！」

translations.literal: Compared with the ancients, I consider myself rather unfortunate!"
translations.idiomatic: Compared with men of old, I consider myself rather unfortunate!

sentences.zh: 德殺之。

translations.literal: De killed him.
translations.idiomatic: De had him executed.

sentences.zh: 遂定都廣固。。

translations.literal: Thereupon he established his capital at Guanggu.
translations.idiomatic: He then established his capital at Guanggu.

sentences.zh: 燕李旱行至建安，燕主盛急召之，君臣莫測其故。

translations.literal: Li Han of Yan had marched as far as Jian'an when the Yan ruler Sheng urgently recalled him; ruler and ministers none could fathom the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han of Yan had marched as far as Jian'an when Murong Sheng urgently recalled him. Neither ruler nor ministers could fathom why.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛未，復遣之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day xinwei, he was sent out again.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinwei day, he was sent out again.

sentences.zh: 李朗聞其家被誅，擁二千餘戶以自固；

translations.literal: Li Lang heard his family had been executed; he gathered more than two thousand households to fortify himself;
translations.idiomatic: Li Lang heard his family had been executed and gathered more than two thousand households to fortify himself;

sentences.zh: 及聞旱還，謂有內變，不復設備，留其子養守令支，自迎魏師於北平。

translations.literal: when he heard Han had returned, he thought there was internal turmoil and no longer made preparations; he left his son Yang to guard Lingzhi and himself went to meet Wei troops at Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: when he heard Li Han had returned, he assumed there was internal turmoil and stopped making preparations. He left his son Yang to hold Lingzhi and went himself to meet Wei troops at Beiping.

sentences.zh: 壬子，旱襲令支，克之，遣廣威將軍孟廣平追及朗於無終，斬之。。

translations.literal: On the day renzi, Han attacked Lingzhi, took it, and dispatched the General of Expansive Might Meng Guangping to pursue and overtake Lang at Wuzhong and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day, Li Han stormed Lingzhi and captured it. He sent General of Expansive Might Meng Guangping in pursuit; Meng caught Li Lang at Wuzhong and executed him.

sentences.zh: 秦主興以災異屢見，降號稱王，下詔令群公、卿士、將牧、守宰各降一等；

translations.literal: The Qin ruler Xing, because calamities and portents repeatedly appeared, lowered his title and styled himself king; he issued an edict ordering the dukes, ministers, generals, governors, and local officials each to lower one rank;
translations.idiomatic: Because calamities and portents kept appearing, the Qin ruler Yao Xing lowered his title to king and issued an edict that dukes, ministers, generals, governors, and local officials should each demote themselves one rank;

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元弘始。

translations.literal: he proclaimed a great amnesty and changed the reign title to Hongshi.
translations.idiomatic: he proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Hongshi.

sentences.zh: 存問孤貧，舉拔賢俊，簡省法令，清察獄訟，守令之有政跡者賞之，貪殘者誅之，遠近肅然。。

translations.literal: He inquired after orphans and the poor, promoted worthy men, simplified laws, cleared and examined prison cases, rewarded prefects and magistrates with good records in office, executed the greedy and cruel, and near and far were awed into order.
translations.idiomatic: He sent relief to orphans and the poor, promoted talented men, streamlined the laws, and reviewed court cases. Officials with good records were rewarded and the greedy and cruel were executed. Order was restored near and far.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲午，燕中衛將軍衛雙有罪，賜死。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jiawu, Wei Shuang, Central Guard General of Yan, was guilty and granted death.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiawu day, Wei Shuang, Central Guard General of Yan, was found guilty and ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 李旱還，聞雙死，懼，棄軍而亡，至板陘，復還歸罪。

translations.literal: Li Han returned, heard Shuang was dead, feared, abandoned the army and fled; reaching Banshi, he returned again to accept punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han was on his way back when he learned of Shuang's death. In fear he abandoned his army and fled. At Banshi he turned back and surrendered himself to judgment.

sentences.zh: 燕主盛復其爵位，謂侍中孫勍曰：「旱為將而棄軍，罪在不赦。

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Sheng restored his rank and title and said to Attendant-in-Ordinary Sun Qing: "Han as general abandoned the army—crime unpardonable.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Sheng restored his rank and title and said to Attendant-in-Ordinary Sun Qing, "As a general Han abandoned his army. That is an unpardonable crime.

sentences.zh: 然昔先帝蒙塵，骨肉離心，公卿失節，惟旱以宦者忠勤不懈，始終如一，故吾念其功而赦之耳。。

translations.literal: Yet in the past the former emperor suffered exile; flesh and blood turned against one another, ministers lost their integrity—only Han as eunuch was loyal and diligent without slackening, from beginning to end one-minded; so I recall his merit and pardon him, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the former emperor suffered exile, kin turned against kin and ministers betrayed their posts. Only Han, though a eunuch, served with unwavering loyalty from first to last. I pardon him in remembrance of that service.

sentences.zh: 辛恭靖固守百餘日，魏救未至，秦兵拔洛陽，獲恭靖。

translations.literal: Xin Gongjing held firm for more than a hundred days; Wei relief had not arrived; Qin troops took Luoyang and captured Gongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Gongjing held out for more than a hundred days, but Wei relief never came. Qin forces took Luoyang and captured him.

sentences.zh: 恭靖見秦王興，不拜，曰：「吾不為羌賊臣！」

translations.literal: Gongjing saw the Qin king Xing, did not bow, and said: "I will not be minister to the Di bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: When brought before King Yao Xing of Qin, Gongjing refused to bow. "I will never serve Di bandits!" he declared.

sentences.zh: 興囚之，恭靖逃歸。

translations.literal: Xing imprisoned him; Gongjing escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xing had him imprisoned, but Gongjing escaped and made his way back.

sentences.zh: 自淮、漢以北，諸城多請降，送任於秦。。

translations.literal: From the Huai and Han northward, many cities requested surrender and sent hostages to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Huai and Han rivers, city after city offered surrender and sent hostages to Qin.

sentences.zh: 魏主珪以穆崇為豫州刺史，鎮野王。。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler Gui appointed Mu Chong Governor of Yuzhou, stationed at Yewang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Tuoba Gui of Wei appointed Mu Chong Governor of Yuzhou and posted him at Yewang.

sentences.zh: 會稽世子元顯，性苛刻，生殺任意；

translations.literal: The Heir of Kuaiji, Yuanxian, was harsh by nature, killing and sparing at will;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yuanxian, heir of Kuaiji, was harsh by nature and killed or spared as he pleased;

sentences.zh: 發東土諸郡免奴為客者，號曰樂屬，移置京師，以充兵役，東土囂然苦之。。

translations.literal: he summoned from the eastern lands all freed slaves who had become clients, calling them Music Retainers, moved them to the capital to fill military service, and the eastern lands were uproariously distressed.
translations.idiomatic: he conscripted freed slaves who had become tenant clients from the eastern commanderies, called them "Music Retainers," and relocated them to the capital for military service. The eastern provinces erupted in outrage.

sentences.zh: 孫恩因民心騷動，自海島帥其黨殺上虞令，遂攻會稽。

translations.literal: Sun En, taking advantage of popular unrest, led his followers from the sea island, killed the Magistrate of Shangyu, and then attacked Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En seized on the unrest. Leading his followers from their island base, he killed the magistrate of Shangyu and marched on Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 會稽內史王凝之，羲之之子也，世奉天師道，不出兵，亦不設備，日於道室稽顙跪咒。

translations.literal: Wang Ningzhi, Internal Grandee of Kuaiji and son of Xizhi, for generations practiced the Celestial Masters Way; he dispatched no troops, made no preparations, and daily in the Dao chamber kowtowed and knelt in incantation.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ningzhi, Internal Grandee of Kuaiji and son of Wang Xizhi, came from a family devoted to the Celestial Masters faith. He sent out no troops and made no defense, spending his days kowtowing and chanting in the ritual hall.

sentences.zh: 官屬請出兵討恩，凝之曰：「我已請大道，借鬼兵守諸津要，各數萬，賊不足憂也。」

translations.literal: Officials asked to dispatch troops against En; Ningzhi said: "I have already prayed to the Great Way and borrowed ghost soldiers to guard the passes—each several tens of thousands; the bandits are nothing to worry about."
translations.idiomatic: When his staff urged him to march against En, Ningzhi said, "I have already invoked the Great Way and borrowed ghost soldiers to hold every pass—tens of thousands at each. The rebels are nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 及恩漸近，乃聽出兵，恩已至郡下。

translations.literal: When En gradually drew near, only then did he permit troops to go out; En had already reached below the commandery seat.
translations.idiomatic: Only when En drew near did he allow troops to march out—by then En was already at the gates of the city.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，恩陷會稽，凝之出走，恩執而殺之，並其諸子。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, En took Kuaiji; Ningzhi fled; En seized and killed him, along with all his sons.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day En captured Kuaiji. Ningzhi fled but was seized and executed, together with all his sons.

sentences.zh: 凝之妻謝道韫，奕之女也，聞寇至，舉措自若，命婢肩輿，抽刀出門，手殺數人，乃被執。

translations.literal: Ningzhi's wife Xie Daoyun, daughter of Yi, when she heard the raiders had come, conducted herself calmly, ordered a maid to carry a sedan chair, drew a knife and went out the gate, killed several men with her own hand, and then was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzhi's wife Xie Daoyun, daughter of Xie Yi, heard the enemy was coming and showed no panic. She had a maid carry her in a sedan chair, drew a blade, went out the gate, and killed several men herself before she was captured.

sentences.zh: 吳國內史桓謙、臨海太守新秦王崇、義興太守魏隱皆棄郡走。

translations.literal: Huan Qian, Internal Grandee of Wu, Wang Chong, Administrator of Linhai and Prince of Xin, and Wei Yin, Administrator of Yixing, all abandoned their commanderies and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Qian, Internal Grandee of Wu; Wang Chong, Prince of Xin and Administrator of Linhai; and Wei Yin, Administrator of Yixing—all abandoned their posts and fled.

sentences.zh: 於是會稽謝金鹹，吳郡陸瑰、吳興丘尪、義興許充之、臨海周冑、永嘉張永等及東陽、新安凡八郡人，一時起兵，殺長吏以應恩，旬日之中，眾數十萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xie Jin of Kuaiji, Lu Gui of Wu Commandery, Qiu Kuang of Wuxing, Xu Chongzhi of Yixing, Zhou Zhou of Linhai, Zhang Yong of Yongjia, and others, together with the people of Dongyang and Xin'an—eight commanderies in all—at once raised troops, killed chief officials to respond to En, and within ten days followers numbered several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Then Xie Jin of Kuaiji, Lu Gui of Wu, Qiu Kuang of Wuxing, Xu Chongzhi of Yixing, Zhou Zhou of Linhai, Zhang Yong of Yongjia, and others across eight commanderies including Dongyang and Xin'an rose at once, killed their local officials, and joined En. Within ten days their forces numbered in the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 吳興太守謝邈、永嘉太守司馬逸、嘉興公顧胤、南康公謝明慧、黃門郎謝沖、張琨、中書郎孔道等皆為恩黨所殺。

translations.literal: Xie Miao, Administrator of Wuxing; Sima Yi, Administrator of Yongjia; Gu Yin, Duke of Jiaxing; Xie Minghui, Duke of Nankang; Xie Chong and Zhang Kun, Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate; Kong Dao, Secretariat Officer; and others were all killed by En's followers.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Miao, Administrator of Wuxing; Sima Yi, Administrator of Yongjia; Gu Yin, Duke of Jiaxing; Xie Minghui, Duke of Nankang; Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate Xie Chong and Zhang Kun; Secretariat Officer Kong Dao; and others were all killed by En's partisans.

sentences.zh: 邈、沖，皆安之弟子也。

translations.literal: Miao and Chong were both disciples of An.
translations.idiomatic: Miao and Chong were both disciples of Xie An.

sentences.zh: 時三吳承平日久，民不習戰，故郡縣兵皆望風奔潰。

translations.literal: At that time the Three Wu regions had enjoyed peace long; the people were unaccustomed to war; therefore commandery and county troops all fled at the mere sight of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Wu region had known peace for so long that the people were unused to war. Commandery and county troops fled at the first sight of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 恩據會稽，自稱征東將軍，逼人士為官屬，號其黨曰「長生人」，民有不與之同者，戮及嬰孩，死者什七、八。

translations.literal: En occupied Kuaiji, styled himself General Who Conquers the East, forced gentry to serve as officials, called his followers "Long-lived Men"; among the people those who would not join—slaughter extended to infants; seven or eight in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: En seized Kuaiji, styled himself General Who Conquers the East, and forced local notables into office. He called his followers "Long-lived Men." Those who refused to join were slaughtered down to infants; seven or eight out of ten perished.

sentences.zh: 醢諸縣令以食其妻子，不肯食者，輒支解之。

translations.literal: He pickled the various magistrates for their wives and children to eat; those who refused to eat were at once dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: He had magistrates minced and forced their wives and children to eat the flesh. Those who refused were dismembered on the spot.

sentences.zh: 所過掠財物，燒邑屋，焚倉廩，刊木，堙井，相帥聚於會稽；

translations.literal: Wherever he passed he plundered goods, burned towns and houses, torched granaries, felled trees, filled wells, and leaders gathered at Kuaiji;
translations.idiomatic: Wherever they marched they looted, burned towns and granaries, felled trees, and filled in wells, driving the population to gather at Kuaiji;

sentences.zh: 婦人有嬰兒不能去者，投於水中，曰：「賀汝先登仙堂，我當尋後就汝。」

translations.literal: women with infants who could not leave were thrown into the water, saying: "Congratulations on ascending the Immortal Hall first—I shall follow after to join you."
translations.idiomatic: women who could not flee with their infants were thrown into the water with the words, "Congratulations on reaching the immortal halls first—I will follow soon.

sentences.zh: 恩表會稽王道子及世子元顯之罪，請誅之。。

translations.literal: En memorialized the crimes of the Prince of Kuaiji Daozi and the heir Yuanxian, requesting their execution.
translations.idiomatic: En submitted a memorial listing the crimes of Prince Sima Daozi of Kuaiji and his heir Yuanxian and calling for their execution.

sentences.zh: 自帝即位以來，內外乖異，石頭以南皆為荊、江所據，以西皆豫州所專，京口及江北皆劉牢之及廣陵相同雅之所制，朝廷所行，惟三吳而已。

translations.literal: Since the emperor's accession, inside and outside had been at odds; south of Shitou all was held by Jing and Jiang; westward all was monopolized by Yuzhou; Jingkou and north of the river were all controlled by Liu Laozhi and the Inspector of Guangling Xiang Ya; what the court could enforce extended only to the Three Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Since the emperor's accession, court and provinces had fallen out of step. South of Shitou was held by the Jing and Jiang regions; westward lay Yuzhou's domain; Jingkou and the lands north of the Yangzi were controlled by Liu Laozhi and Xiang Ya, Inspector of Guangling. The court's authority reached no farther than the Three Wu.

sentences.zh: 及孫恩作亂，八郡皆為恩有，畿內諸縣，盜賊處處蜂起，恩黨亦有潛伏在建康者，人情危懼。

translations.literal: When Sun En rebelled, eight commanderies all fell to En; within the capital region bandits rose everywhere like swarming bees; En's followers also lurked hidden in Jiankang; morale was fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun En rebelled, eight commanderies fell to him. Bandits rose everywhere in the capital region, and his agents were known to be hiding in Jiankang itself. Fear spread through the population.

sentences.zh: 常慮竊發，於是內外戒嚴。

translations.literal: Constant fear of sudden outbreak; thereupon inside and outside were placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a sudden uprising, the court put the capital and its environs under strict guard.

sentences.zh: 加道子黃鉞，元為領中軍將軍，命徐州刺史謝琰兼督吳興、義興軍事以討恩；

translations.literal: Daozi was given the yellow battle-axe; Yuan was made General Who Leads the Army of the Center; the court ordered Xie Yan, Governor of Xuzhou, to concurrently supervise military affairs of Wuxing and Yixing to attack En;
translations.idiomatic: Daozi was granted the yellow battle-axe; Yuanxian was made General Who Leads the Army of the Center; and Xie Yan, Governor of Xuzhou, was ordered to take command of Wuxing and Yixing and march against En;

sentences.zh: 劉牢之亦發兵討恩，拜表輒行。。

translations.literal: Liu Laozhi also dispatched troops against En, submitted his memorial and immediately marched.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi also mobilized against En, submitting his memorial and marching at once.

sentences.zh: 西秦以金城太守辛靜為右丞相。。

translations.literal: Western Qin appointed Xin Jing, Administrator of Jincheng, Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Western Qin appointed Xin Jing, Administrator of Jincheng, as Right Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲午，燕燕郡太守高湖帥戶三千降魏。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day jiawu, Gao Hu, Administrator of Yan Commandery under Yan, led three thousand households in surrender to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiawu day, Gao Hu, Administrator of Yan Commandery under Yan, surrendered to Wei with three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 湖，泰之子也。。

translations.literal: Hu was Tai's son.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Hu was the son of Gao Tai.

sentences.zh: 丙午，燕主盛封弟淵為章武公，虔為博陵公，子定為遼西公。。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, the Yan ruler Sheng enfeoffed his younger brother Yuan as Duke of Zhangwu, Qian as Duke of Boling, and his son Ding as Duke of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day Murong Sheng enfeoffed his younger brother Murong Yuan as Duke of Zhangwu, Murong Qian as Duke of Boling, and his son Murong Ding as Duke of Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 丁未，燕太后段氏卒，謚曰惠德皇后。。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, Empress Dowager Duan of Yan died; her posthumous title was Empress Hui and Virtuous.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day Empress Dowager Duan of Yan died. She was posthumously titled Empress Hui and Virtuous.

sentences.zh: 謝琰擊斬許允之，迎魏隱還郡，進擊丘尪，破之，與劉牢之轉斗而前，所向輒克。

translations.literal: Xie Yan attacked and beheaded Xu Yunzhi, welcomed Wei Yin back to the commandery, advanced to attack Qiu Kuang and defeated him; with Liu Laozhi he fought as they advanced, wherever they went they conquered.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yan attacked and killed Xu Chongzhi, restored Wei Yin to his commandery, and advanced against Qiu Kuang and routed him. He and Liu Laozhi fought their way forward, conquering wherever they turned.

sentences.zh: 琰留屯烏程，遣司馬高素助牢之，進臨浙江。

translations.literal: Yan remained stationed at Wucheng, sent Marshal Gao Su to assist Laozhi, and advanced to the Zhe River.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yan held at Wucheng and sent Marshal Gao Su to reinforce Laozhi, advancing as far as the Zhe River.

sentences.zh: 詔以牢之都督吳都諸軍事。。

translations.literal: An edict made Laozhi overall commander of all military affairs of the Wu capital region.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Liu Laozhi overall commander of military affairs in the Wu region.

sentences.zh: 初，彭城劉裕，生而母死，父翹僑居京口，家貧，將棄之。

translations.literal: Initially, Liu Yu of Pengcheng—at birth his mother died; his father Qiao lived as an émigré at Jingkou; the family was poor and about to abandon him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liu Yu of Pengcheng lost his mother at birth. His father Liu Qiao, an émigré living at Jingkou, was so poor that he was about to abandon the infant.

sentences.zh: 同郡劉懷敬之母，裕之從母也，生懷敬未期，走往救之，斷懷敬乳而乳之。

translations.literal: The mother of Liu Huaijing of the same commandery was Yu's maternal aunt; Huaijing was not yet one year old when she ran to save him, stopped Huaijing's nursing and nursed Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The mother of Liu Huaijing of the same commandery—Yu's aunt—had just given birth to Huaijing. She ran to the rescue, weaned her own child, and nursed Yu instead.

sentences.zh: 及長，勇健有大志。

translations.literal: When grown, he was bold and strong with great ambition.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he was bold, vigorous, and full of ambition.

sentences.zh: 僅識文字，以賣履為業，好樗蒲，為鄉閭所賤。

translations.literal: He knew barely any characters, made his living selling shoes, loved gambling, and was despised by the village.
translations.idiomatic: He knew only a few written characters, made a living selling straw sandals, loved gambling, and was looked down on in his neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 劉牢之擊孫恩，引裕參軍事，使將數十人覘賊。

translations.literal: When Liu Laozhi attacked Sun En, he brought Yu into military affairs and had him lead several dozen men to scout the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Laozhi marched against Sun En, he took Yu onto his staff and sent him with a few dozen men to reconnoiter the enemy.

sentences.zh: 遇賊數千人，即迎擊之，從者皆死，裕墜岸下。

translations.literal: They encountered several thousand bandits; he immediately met them in attack; his followers all died; Yu fell off the bank below.
translations.idiomatic: They ran into several thousand rebels. Yu charged at once. His men were all killed and he fell from the bank.

sentences.zh: 賊臨岸欲下，裕奮長刀仰斫殺數人，乃得登岸，仍大呼逐之，賊皆走，裕所殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: The bandits on the bank were about to descend; Yu wielded a long knife and upward cut down several men, then got onto the bank; still shouting he pursued them; the bandits all fled; those Yu killed and wounded were very many.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels leaned over the bank to finish him, Yu swung his long blade upward and cut down several men, then scrambled ashore. Shouting, he drove them off. He killed and wounded a great many.

sentences.zh: 劉敬宣怪裕久不返，引兵尋之，見裕獨驅數千人，鹹共歎息。

translations.literal: Liu Jingxuan wondered that Yu had long not returned, led troops to seek him, saw Yu alone driving off several thousand, and all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jingxuan, alarmed that Yu had not returned, led men to find him and saw Yu alone putting thousands of rebels to flight. All who watched sighed in wonder.

sentences.zh: 因進擊賊，大破之，斬獲千餘人。。

translations.literal: Thereupon they advanced against the bandits, greatly defeated them, and killed and captured more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed the attack, routed the rebels, and killed or captured more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 初，恩聞八郡響應，謂其屬曰：「天下無復事矣，當與諸君朝服至建康。」

translations.literal: Initially, when En heard eight commanderies had responded, he said to his followers: "Under Heaven there is no more business to settle—we shall with you all in court dress go to Jiankang."
translations.idiomatic: When En first heard that eight commanderies had risen with him, he told his followers, "The empire is ours. We shall dress in court robes and march on Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 既而聞牢之臨江，曰：「我割浙江以東，不失作句踐！」

translations.literal: Then when he heard Laozhi was at the river, he said: "I will cut off the lands east of the Zhe River—I shall not fail to play Goujian!"
translations.idiomatic: But when he learned that Laozhi had reached the river, he said, "If I hold everything east of the Zhe, I can still play the part of Goujian!

sentences.zh: 戊申，牢之引兵濟江，恩聞之，曰：「孤不羞走。」

translations.literal: On the day wushen, Laozhi led troops across the river; when En heard it, he said: "I am not ashamed to flee."
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day Laozhi crossed the river with his army. When En heard of it he said, "I am not too proud to run.

sentences.zh: 遂驅男女二十餘萬口東走，多棄寶物、子女於道，官軍競取之，恩由是得脫，復逃入海島。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drove men and women numbering more than two hundred thousand eastward; many abandoned treasures and children on the road; government troops competed to take them; En thereby escaped and again fled to the sea island.
translations.idiomatic: He then drove more than two hundred thousand men, women, and children eastward, abandoning treasures and children along the road. Government troops stopped to loot the spoils, and En slipped away and fled back to his island refuge.

sentences.zh: 高素破恩黨於山陰，斬恩所署吳郡太守陸瑰、吳興太守丘尪、餘姚令吳興沈穆夫。。

translations.literal: Gao Su defeated En's followers at Shanyin and beheaded Lu Gui, Administrator of Wu Commandery appointed by En; Qiu Kuang, Administrator of Wuxing; and Shen Mufu of Wuxing, Magistrate of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Su routed En's partisans at Shanyin and executed Lu Gui, En's appointee as Administrator of Wu; Qiu Kuang, Administrator of Wuxing; and Shen Mufu, Magistrate of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 東土遭亂，企望官軍之至，既而牢之等縱軍士暴掠，士民失望，郡縣城中無復人跡，月餘乃稍有還者。

translations.literal: The eastern lands had suffered turmoil and hoped for the arrival of government troops; then Laozhi and the others let soldiers plunder wildly; gentry and people were disappointed; in commandery and county cities there was no longer any human trace; after more than a month slightly some returned.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern provinces, ravaged by rebellion, had looked to the imperial armies for deliverance. Instead Laozhi and his men let their soldiers loot at will. The people lost hope. Towns stood empty for more than a month before anyone ventured back.

sentences.zh: 朝廷憂恩復至，以謝琰為會稽太守、都督五郡軍事，帥徐州文武戍海浦。。

translations.literal: The court feared En would return; it made Xie Yan Administrator of Kuaiji and overall commander of military affairs of five commanderies, leading Xuzhou civil and military officials to garrison the seacoast.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing En might return, the court appointed Xie Yan Administrator of Kuaiji and overall commander of five commanderies, and posted the civil and military officials of Xuzhou to guard the coast.

sentences.zh: 以元顯錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Yuanxian was made Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian was appointed Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時人謂道子為東錄，元顯為西錄；

translations.literal: People of the time called Daozi the Eastern Recorder and Yuanxian the Western Recorder;
translations.idiomatic: People of the day called Daozi the Eastern Recorder and Yuanxian the Western Recorder;

sentences.zh: 西府車騎填湊，東第門可張羅矣。

translations.literal: the Western quarter's carriages and horses packed tight; at the Eastern mansion's gate one could spread a net.
translations.idiomatic: the Western offices thronged with carriages and horses, while at the Eastern residence one could spread a net at the gate—for no one came.

sentences.zh: 元顯無良師友，所親信者率皆佞諛之人，或以為一時英傑，或以為風流名士。

translations.literal: Yuanxian had no good teachers or friends; those he trusted were mostly flatterers—some considered one-time heroes, some considered elegant literati.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian had no worthy mentors. Those he trusted were mostly sycophants whom some hailed as heroes of the age and others as fashionable men of letters.

sentences.zh: 由是元顯日益驕侈，諷禮官立議，以己德隆望重，既錄百揆，百揆皆應盡敬。

translations.literal: Thereby Yuanxian daily grew more arrogant and extravagant; he prompted the rites officials to debate, holding that his virtue was lofty and his fame weighty, and since he recorded all affairs of state, all affairs of state should fully show respect.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian grew ever more arrogant and extravagant. He urged the masters of ceremony to rule that, given his lofty virtue and heavy reputation, and since he now oversaw all government, every minister owed him full deference.

sentences.zh: 於是公卿以下，見元顯皆拜。

translations.literal: Thereupon from dukes and ministers downward, all who saw Yuanxian bowed.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on, every official down to the lowest rank bowed when meeting Yuanxian.

sentences.zh: 時軍旅數起，國用虛竭，自司徒以下，日廩七升，而元顯聚斂不已，富逾帝室。。

translations.literal: At the time campaigns arose repeatedly and state funds were exhausted; from the Steward on down the daily grain ration was seven sheng, yet Yuanxian amassed without cease and his wealth exceeded the imperial house.
