translations.idiomatic: Campaign followed campaign until the treasury was drained. Officials from the Steward downward received seven sheng of grain a day, while Yuanxian kept hoarding wealth until he was richer than the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 殷仲堪恐桓玄跋扈，乃與楊佺期結昏為援。

translations.literal: Yin Zhongkan feared Huan Xuan's overbearing arrogance and therefore allied by marriage with Yang Quanqi as support.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongkan, fearing Huan Xuan's overbearing ambition, sealed an alliance through marriage with Yang Quanqi.

sentences.zh: 佺期屢欲攻玄，仲堪每抑止之。

translations.literal: Quanqi repeatedly wanted to attack Xuan; Zhongkan each time restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi repeatedly urged an attack on Xuan, but Zhongkan always held him back.

sentences.zh: 玄恐終為殷、楊所滅，乃告執政，求廣其所統；

translations.literal: Xuan feared he would ultimately be destroyed by Yin and Yang; he reported to those in power and requested expansion of what he commanded;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, fearing he would eventually be destroyed by Yin and Yang, appealed to the regents and asked for an enlargement of his command;

sentences.zh: 執政亦欲交構，使之乖離，乃加玄都督荊州四郡軍事，又以玄兄偉代佺期兄廣為南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: those in power also wished to sow discord and make them split apart; thereupon they added Xuan as overall commander of military affairs of four commanderies of Jingzhou, and also had Xuan's elder brother Wei replace Quanqi's elder brother Guang as Colonel of the Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: the regents, hoping to drive a wedge between them, made Xuan overall commander of four Jingzhou commanderies and replaced Quanqi's brother Guang as Colonel of the Southern Man with Xuan's brother Huan Wei.

sentences.zh: 佺期忿懼。

translations.literal: Quanqi was angry and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi was furious and afraid.

sentences.zh: 楊廣欲拒桓偉，仲堪不聽，出廣為宜都、建平二郡太守。

translations.literal: Yang Guang wanted to resist Huan Wei; Zhongkan would not listen and sent Guang out as Administrator of the two commanderies of Yidu and Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guang wanted to resist Huan Wei, but Zhongkan refused and posted Guang as Administrator of Yidu and Jianping.

sentences.zh: 楊孜敬先為江夏相，玄以兵襲而劫之，以為咨議參軍。。

translations.literal: Yang Zijing had previously been Chancellor of Jiangxia; Xuan with troops raided and seized him and made him Consultation Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zijing had been Chancellor of Jiangxia. Xuan attacked by force, seized him, and made him a Consultation Adviser.

sentences.zh: 佺期勒兵建牙，聲雲援洛，欲與仲堪共襲玄。

translations.literal: Quanqi mustered troops and raised his banner, proclaiming that he would relieve Luoyang, intending with Zhongkan jointly to raid Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi mobilized his army and raised his standard, claiming he would march to relieve Luoyang, and planned to strike Xuan together with Zhongkan.

sentences.zh: 仲堪雖外結佺期而內疑其心，苦止之；

translations.literal: Zhongkan though outwardly allied with Quanqi inwardly doubted his heart and painfully restrained him;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan had allied with Quanqi outwardly but distrusted him inwardly and tried hard to stop him;

sentences.zh: 猶虎弗能禁，遣從弟遹屯於北境，以遏佺期。

translations.literal: still like a tiger unable to restrain, he sent his younger cousin Yu to encamp on the northern border to block Quanqi.
translations.idiomatic: unable to restrain him fully, he sent his cousin Yin Yu to encamp on the northern frontier to block Quanqi.

sentences.zh: 佺期既不能獨舉，又不測仲堪本意，乃解兵。。

translations.literal: Quanqi could neither act alone nor fathom Zhongkan's true intent; thereupon he disbanded his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi could neither move alone nor read Zhongkan's true intentions, and so he stood down.

sentences.zh: 仲堪多疑少決，咨議參軍羅企生謂其弟遵生曰：「殷侯仁而無斷，必及於難。

translations.literal: Zhongkan was suspicious and slow to decide; Consultation Adviser Luo Qisheng said to his younger brother Zunsheng: "Lord Yin is benevolent but without decisiveness—he must meet calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan was indecisive and mistrustful. Consultation Adviser Luo Qisheng told his brother Zunsheng, "Lord Yin is kind but cannot decide. Disaster will find him.

sentences.zh: 吾蒙知遇，義不可去，必將死之。」。

translations.literal: I have received his favor; duty cannot allow me to leave—I must die for him."
translations.idiomatic: He has treated me well. It would be wrong to abandon him. I shall die at his side."

sentences.zh: 是歲，荊州大水，平地三丈，仲堪竭倉廩以賑饑民。

translations.literal: That year, Jing Province suffered great flooding; on level ground the water stood three zhang deep; Zhongkan emptied the granaries to relieve the hungry people.
translations.idiomatic: That year Jing Province was devastated by floods three zhang deep even on flat ground. Zhongkan emptied the granaries to feed the starving.

sentences.zh: 桓玄欲乘其虛而伐之，乃發兵西上，亦聲言救洛，與仲堪書曰：「佺期受國恩而棄山陵，宜共罪之。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan wished to take advantage of their weakness to attack them; thereupon he dispatched troops westward, also proclaiming he would relieve Luoyang, and wrote to Zhongkan saying: "Quanqi received the state's grace yet abandoned the imperial tombs—we should join in condemning him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan wanted to strike while they were vulnerable. He marched west, again claiming he would relieve Luoyang, and wrote to Zhongkan: "Quanqi enjoyed the state's favor yet abandoned the imperial tombs. We should condemn him together.

sentences.zh: 今當入沔討除佺期，已頓兵江口。

translations.literal: Now I am about to enter the Mian region to suppress and eliminate Quanqi; I have already halted troops at the river mouth.
translations.idiomatic: I am marching into the Mian basin to destroy Quanqi and have already encamped at the river mouth.

sentences.zh: 若見與無貳，可收楊廣殺之；

translations.literal: If you see that we have no duplicity, you may seize Yang Guang and kill him;
translations.idiomatic: If you stand with me without wavering, seize Yang Guang and kill him.

sentences.zh: 如其不爾，便當帥兵入江。」

translations.literal: If it is not so, then I shall lead troops into the Jiang."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I shall lead my army into the Yangtze basin."

sentences.zh: 時巴陵有積穀，玄先遣兵襲取之。

translations.literal: At that time Baling had accumulated grain; Xuan first sent troops to raid and seize it.
translations.idiomatic: Baling meanwhile held a large grain reserve. Xuan sent troops first to seize it by surprise.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史郭銓當之官，路經夏口，玄詐稱朝廷遣銓為己前鋒，乃授以江夏之眾，使督軍諸軍並進，密報兄偉令為內應。

translations.literal: Liang Province Inspector Guo Quan was about to assume office; passing through Xiakou on the way, Xuan falsely claimed the court had sent Quan as his vanguard; thereupon he gave him the forces of Jiangxia, had him supervise the armies as all advanced together, and secretly reported to his elder brother Wei to act as inner support.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Quan, newly appointed Inspector of Liang Province, was traveling through Xiakou on his way to take office. Xuan falsely claimed the court had posted Quan as his vanguard, put the Jiangxia forces under his command, and ordered a general advance while secretly telling his brother Wei to rise within as an ally.

sentences.zh: 偉遑遽不知所為，自繼疏示仲堪。

translations.literal: Wei, flustered, did not know what to do; he himself continued the memorial and showed it to Zhongkan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, in panic, did not know what to do. He forwarded the message himself and showed it to Zhongkan.

sentences.zh: 仲堪執偉為質，令與玄書，辭甚苦至。

translations.literal: Zhongkan seized Wei as a hostage, had him write to Xuan; the words were very bitter and earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan took Wei hostage and made him write to Xuan in the most anguished terms.

sentences.zh: 玄曰：「仲堪為人無決，常懷成敗之計，為兒子作慮，我兄必無憂也。。

translations.literal: Xuan said: "Zhongkan as a man has no decisiveness; he constantly harbors calculations of success and failure, makes plans for his sons—my elder brother surely need not worry.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan said, "Zhongkan cannot decide. He is always weighing gain and loss and scheming for his sons. My brother has nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 仲堪遣殷遹帥水軍七千至西江口，玄使郭銓、苻宏擊之，遹等敗走。

translations.literal: Zhongkan sent Yin Yu leading seven thousand river troops to Xijiangkou; Xuan had Guo Quan and Fu Hong attack them; Yu and the others were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan sent Yin Yu with seven thousand river troops to Xijiangkou. Xuan ordered Guo Quan and Fu Hong to attack. Yu was routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 玄頓巴陵，食其谷；

translations.literal: Xuan halted at Baling and ate its grain;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan encamped at Baling and fed his army from its grain;

sentences.zh: 仲堪遣楊廣及弟子道護等拒之，皆為玄所敗。

translations.literal: Zhongkan sent Yang Guang and his nephews Daohu and others to resist; all were defeated by Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan sent Yang Guang and his nephew Daohu and others to hold them off. Xuan defeated them all.

sentences.zh: 江陵震駭。

translations.literal: Jiangling was shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling was seized with terror.

sentences.zh: 城中乏食，以胡麻廩軍士。

translations.literal: In the city food was scarce; they used sesame to supply the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Food in the city ran short, and the troops were rationed on sesame.

sentences.zh: 玄乘勝至零口，去江陵二十里，仲堪急召楊佺期以自救。

translations.literal: Xuan, riding victory, reached Lingkou, twenty li from Jiangling; Zhongkan urgently summoned Yang Quanqi to save himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan pressed his advantage to Lingkou, twenty li from Jiangling. Zhongkan urgently called on Yang Quanqi to rescue him.

sentences.zh: 佺期曰：「江陵無食，何以待敵！

translations.literal: Quanqi said: "Jiangling has no food—how can we face the enemy!
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi said, "Jiangling has no provisions. How can we hold off the enemy?

sentences.zh: 可來見就，共守襄陽。」

translations.literal: You can come to me; let us together defend Xiangyang."
translations.idiomatic: Come join me and we will hold Xiangyang together."

sentences.zh: 仲堪志在全軍保境，不欲棄州逆走，乃紿之曰：「比來收集，已有儲矣。」

translations.literal: Zhongkan's aim was to keep the whole army and defend the borders; he did not wish to abandon the province and flee against the current; thereupon he deceived him saying: "Recently we have gathered supplies—there are already stores."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan wanted to keep his forces intact and defend the province. Unwilling to abandon Jing and flee upstream, he lied: "We have been gathering supplies. We already have stores."

sentences.zh: 佺期信之，帥步騎八千，精甲耀日，至江陵，仲堪唯以飯餉其軍。

translations.literal: Quanqi believed it, led eight thousand infantry and cavalry with brilliant armor shining in the sun, reached Jiangling; Zhongkan could only supply his army with plain rice.
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi believed him and marched in with eight thousand foot and horse, their fine armor blazing in the sun. Zhongkan could offer his army nothing but plain rice.

sentences.zh: 佺期大怒曰：「今茲敗矣！」

translations.literal: Quanqi said in great anger: "This time we are ruined!"
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi flew into a rage. "We are ruined!"

sentences.zh: 不見仲堪，與其兄廣共擊玄。

translations.literal: He did not see Zhongkan; with his elder brother Guang he jointly attacked Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to see Zhongkan and, with his brother Guang, attacked Xuan together.

sentences.zh: 玄畏其銳，退軍馬頭。

translations.literal: Xuan feared their sharpness and withdrew his army to Matou.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, wary of their momentum, pulled back to Matou.

sentences.zh: 明日，佺期引兵急擊郭銓，幾獲之。

translations.literal: The next day, Quanqi led troops in fierce attack on Guo Quan and nearly captured him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Quanqi launched a furious assault on Guo Quan and nearly took him.

sentences.zh: 會玄兵至，佺期大敗，單騎奔襄陽。

translations.literal: Just then Xuan's troops arrived; Quanqi was greatly defeated and fled alone on horseback to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Then Xuan's reinforcements arrived. Quanqi was routed and fled alone to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 仲堪出奔酇城。

translations.literal: Zhongkan fled out to Zuo City.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan fled to Zuo City.

sentences.zh: 玄遣將軍馮該追佺期及廣，皆獲而殺之，傳首建康。

translations.literal: Xuan sent General Feng Gai to pursue Quanqi and Guang; both were captured and killed; their heads were sent to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sent General Feng Gai after Quanqi and Guang. Both were captured and killed, and their heads were sent to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 佺期弟思平、從弟尚保、孜敬逃入蠻中。

translations.literal: Quanqi's younger brother Siping, his younger cousins Shangbao and Zijing, fled into the barbarian lands.
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi's brother Siping and his cousins Shangbao and Zijing escaped into the hill country.

sentences.zh: 仲堪聞佺期死，將數百人將奔長安，至冠軍城，該追獲之，還至柞溪，逼令自殺，並殺殷道護。

translations.literal: Zhongkan heard Quanqi was dead; leading several hundred men he was about to flee to Chang'an; reaching Guanjun City, Gai pursued and captured him; returning to Zhaoxi, he forced him to kill himself and also killed Yin Daohu.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongkan learned Quanqi was dead, he set out for Chang'an with a few hundred followers. At Guanjun City Feng Gai overtook and captured him. At Zhaoxi he was forced to take his own life, and Yin Daohu was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 仲堪奉天師道，禱請鬼神，不吝財賄，而嗇於周急。

translations.literal: Zhongkan followed the Way of the Celestial Master, prayed to spirits and gods, was not sparing of wealth and bribes, yet was niggardly in urgent need.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan followed the Way of the Celestial Master, prayed to spirits without stinting gifts, yet was tight-fisted when others were in desperate need.

sentences.zh: 好為小惠以悅人，病者自為診脈分藥，用計倚伏煩密，而短於鑒略，故至於敗。。

translations.literal: He liked to make small favors to please people; for the sick he personally took pulses and dispensed medicine; his use of schemes was intricate in rise and fall, yet he was short in discernment and strategy—therefore he came to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He liked petty favors that won people's hearts, personally diagnosing the sick and dispensing medicine. His schemes were elaborate, but he lacked foresight—and so he fell.

sentences.zh: 仲堪之走也，文武無送者，惟羅企生從之。

translations.literal: When Zhongkan fled, none of the civil and military officials saw him off—only Luo Qisheng followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongkan fled, not one of his officials saw him off. Only Luo Qisheng went with him.

sentences.zh: 路經家門，弟遵生曰：「作如此分離，何可不一執手！」

translations.literal: Passing his home gate on the road, his younger brother Zunsheng said: "Facing such a parting—how can we not clasp hands once!"
translations.idiomatic: As they passed his home, his brother Zunsheng called out, "On a parting like this, how can we not clasp hands once?"

sentences.zh: 企生旋馬授手，遵生有力，因牽下之，曰；

translations.literal: Qisheng turned his horse and offered his hand; Zunsheng was strong and thereupon pulled him down, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng wheeled his horse and reached out. Zunsheng, a strong man, yanked him from the saddle and said:

sentences.zh: 「家有老母，去將何之？」

translations.literal: " At home there is an old mother—where are you going by leaving?"
translations.idiomatic: " Mother is at home. Where do you think you are going?"

sentences.zh: 企生揮淚曰：「今日之事，我必死之，汝等奉養，不失子道。

translations.literal: Qisheng wiped tears and said: "Today's affair—I must die for it; you all shall support her—you will not fail the way of a son.
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng said through tears, "Today I am bound to die. You will support her—you will not fail in filial duty.

sentences.zh: 一門之中，有忠與孝，亦復何恨！」

translations.literal: Within one household to have both loyalty and filial piety—what more regret is there!"
translations.idiomatic: In one house to have both loyalty and filial piety—what regret could there be!"

sentences.zh: 遵生抱之愈急，仲堪於路待之，見企生無脫理，策馬而去。

translations.literal: Zunsheng held him ever tighter; Zhongkan waited on the road for him; seeing Qisheng had no way to escape, he spurred his horse and left.
translations.idiomatic: Zunsheng held him all the tighter. Zhongkan waited on the road, saw that Qisheng could not break free, and rode on.

sentences.zh: 及玄至，荊州人士無不詣玄者，企生獨不往，而營理仲堪家事。

translations.literal: When Xuan arrived, none of the men of Jing Province failed to call on Xuan—Qisheng alone did not go, but instead put in order Zhongkan's household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan arrived, every notable in Jing Province paid him court—except Qisheng, who stayed away and instead settled Zhongkan's household affairs.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「如此，禍必至矣！」

translations.literal: Someone said: "Like this, calamity is sure to come!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned him, "That way lies disaster!"

sentences.zh: 企生曰：「殷侯遇我以國土，為弟所制，不得隨之共殄丑逆，復何面目就桓求生乎！」

translations.literal: Qisheng said: "Lord Yin treated me as a pillar of the state; constrained by my younger brother I could not follow him to destroy the vile rebel together—what face have I to go to Huan and beg for life!"
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng replied, "Lord Yin honored me as a true servant of the state. Held back by my brother, I could not follow him to destroy this rebel. What face would I have to crawl to Huan for my life?"

sentences.zh: 玄聞之，怒，然待企生素厚，先遣人謂曰：「若謝我，當釋汝。」

translations.literal: Xuan heard it, was angry, yet as he had always treated Qisheng generously, he first sent someone saying: "If you apologize to me, I shall release you."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was angry when he heard, but Qisheng had long been a favorite. He sent word first: "Apologize and I will spare you."

sentences.zh: 企生曰：「吾為殷荊州吏，荊州敗，不能救，尚何謝為！」

translations.literal: Qisheng said: "I am an officer of Lord Yin of Jing Province; Jing Province was defeated and I could not save it—what apology is there to make!"
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng answered, "I served Lord Yin of Jing. Jing fell and I could not save it. What apology do I owe?"

sentences.zh: 玄乃收之，復遣人問企生欲何言。

translations.literal: Xuan thereupon arrested him, and again sent someone to ask what Qisheng wished to say.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had him seized and sent again to ask whether he had any last words.

sentences.zh: 企生曰；

translations.literal: Qisheng said:
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng said:

sentences.zh: 「文帝殺嵇康，嵇紹為晉忠臣。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wen of Wei killed Ji Kang; Ji Shao was a loyal minister of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: " When Emperor Wen of Wei killed Ji Kang, Ji Shao became a loyal minister of Jin.

sentences.zh: 從公乞一弟以養老母！」；

translations.literal: I beg from you one younger brother to support my old mother!"
translations.idiomatic: I beg you for one younger brother to care for our old mother!"

sentences.zh: 玄乃殺企生而赦其弟。。

translations.literal: Xuan thereupon killed Qisheng and pardoned his younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan killed Qisheng and pardoned his brother.

sentences.zh: 涼王光疾甚，立太子紹為天王，自號太上皇帝，以太原公纂為太尉，常山公弘為司徒，謂紹曰；

translations.literal: King Guang of Liang was gravely ill; he installed Crown Prince Shao as Heavenly King, styled himself Retired Emperor, made Prince of Taiyuan Zuan Grand Commandant and Prince of Changshan Hong Minister Over the Masses, and said to Shao:
translations.idiomatic: King Guang of Liang fell gravely ill. He installed Crown Prince Shao as Heavenly King, took the title Retired Emperor, named Prince of Taiyuan Zuan Grand Commandant and Prince of Changshan Hong Minister Over the Masses, and told Shao:

sentences.zh: 「今國家多難，三鄰伺隙，吾沒之後，使纂統六軍，弘管朝政，汝恭己無為，委重二兄，庶幾可濟。

translations.literal: " Now the state has many troubles; three neighbors watch for openings; after my death, have Zuan command the six armies, Hong manage court affairs—you hold yourself respectfully and do nothing, entrust weight to your two elder brothers—perhaps it can be saved.
translations.idiomatic: " The realm is in peril and three neighbors are watching for weakness. After I am gone, let Zuan command the armies and Hong run the court. Hold yourself reverently and leave the weight to your two elder brothers—that may see us through.

sentences.zh: 若內相猜忌，則蕭牆之變，旦夕至矣。」

translations.literal: If within you suspect one another, then turmoil within the palace walls will come morning or evening."
translations.idiomatic: If you turn on one another within, calamity at the palace gates will come any day."

sentences.zh: 又謂纂、弘曰：「永業才非撥亂，直以立嫡有常，猥居元首。

translations.literal: He further said to Zuan and Hong: "Yongye's talent is not for settling chaos—only because establishing the heir has its rule does he undeservedly occupy the chief position.
translations.idiomatic: He told Zuan and Hong, "Yongye is no man to quell chaos. He sits at the head only because the heir has his place.

sentences.zh: 今外有強寇，人心未寧，汝兄弟緝睦，則祚流萬世；

translations.literal: Now outside there are strong foes; men's hearts are not yet settled; if you brothers maintain harmony, then fortune flows for ten thousand generations;
translations.idiomatic: Enemies press from without and the people's hearts are unsettled. If you brothers stay united, the throne may endure for ages;

sentences.zh: 若內自相圖，則禍不旋踵矣。」

translations.literal: if within you plot against one another, then disaster comes without turning the heel."
translations.idiomatic: if you feud among yourselves, ruin will follow at once."

sentences.zh: 纂、弘泣曰：「不敢。」

translations.literal: Zuan and Hong wept and said: "We dare not."
translations.idiomatic: Zuan and Hong wept and said, "We would not dare."

sentences.zh: 又執纂手戒之曰：「汝性粗暴，深為吾憂。

translations.literal: He again grasped Zuan's hand and admonished him saying: "Your nature is rough and violent—this deeply worries me.
translations.idiomatic: Taking Zuan's hand, he warned him, "You are rough by nature. That worries me deeply.

sentences.zh: 善輔永業，勿聽讒言！」

translations.literal: Serve Yongye well; do not heed slander!"
translations.idiomatic: Serve Yongye faithfully. Do not listen to slander!"

sentences.zh: 是日，光卒。

translations.literal: That day, Guang died.
translations.idiomatic: That day Guang died.

sentences.zh: 紹秘不發喪，纂排閣入器，盡哀而出。

translations.literal: Shao concealed the death and did not announce mourning; Zuan pushed open the door and entered the bier chamber, expressed full grief, and came out.
translations.idiomatic: Shao kept the death secret. Zuan forced the door and entered the mourning chamber, wailed his fill, and came out.

sentences.zh: 紹懼，以位讓之，曰：「兄功高年長，宜承大統。」

translations.literal: Shao was afraid and yielded the throne to him, saying: "Elder brother, your merit is high and your years advanced—you should receive the great succession."
translations.idiomatic: Shao, frightened, offered him the throne. "Your merit is great and you are the elder. You should inherit."

sentences.zh: 纂曰：「陛下國之塚嫡，臣敢奸之？」

translations.literal: Zuan said: "Your Majesty is the state's legitimate heir—how dare I usurp it?"
translations.idiomatic: Zuan replied, "Your Majesty is the lawful heir. How could I usurp the throne?"

sentences.zh: 紹固讓，纂不許。

translations.literal: Shao firmly yielded; Zuan would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Shao pressed the offer. Zuan refused.

sentences.zh: 驃騎將軍呂超謂紹曰：「纂為將積年，威震內外，臨喪不安，步高視遠，必有異志，宜早除之。」

translations.literal: Flying Cavalry General Lü Chao said to Shao: "Zuan has been a general for accumulated years; his might shakes within and without; at the mourning he is unsettled, steps high and looks far—he surely has a different intent; he should early be removed."
translations.idiomatic: Flying Cavalry General Lü Chao told Shao, "Zuan has commanded armies for years and his prestige dominates court and camp. At the funeral he is restless, head high and eyes roaming—he harbors treason. Remove him now."

sentences.zh: 紹曰：「先帝言猶在耳，奈何棄之！

translations.literal: Shao said: "The late emperor's words are still in the ears—how can I abandon them!
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "Our father's words still ring in my ears. How can I betray them?

sentences.zh: 吾以弱年負荷大任，方賴二兄以寧家國，縱其圖我，我視死如歸，終不忍有些意也。

translations.literal: I with weak years bear a heavy charge; just now I rely on my two elder brothers to settle family and state; even if he plots against me, I view death as returning home—I ultimately cannot bear to have the slightest intent against him.
translations.idiomatic: I am young and the burden is heavy. I depend on my two elder brothers to keep the house and realm at peace. Even if he plots against me, I am ready to die—and I cannot bring myself to raise a hand against him.

sentences.zh: 卿勿復言！」

translations.literal: You, speak no more!"
translations.idiomatic: Say no more!"

sentences.zh: 纂見紹於湛露堂；

translations.literal: Zuan saw Shao at the Zhanlu Hall;
translations.idiomatic: Zuan visited Shao in the Hall of Pure Dew;

sentences.zh: 超執刀侍側，目纂請收之，紹弗許，超，光弟寶之子也。。

translations.literal: Chao held a blade and waited at the side, signaled with his eyes to Zuan requesting to seize him; Shao would not permit it; Chao was the son of Guang's younger brother Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Chao stood at his side with a sword, signaling Zuan to seize him. Shao refused. Chao was the son of Guang's brother Bao.

sentences.zh: 弘密遣尚書姜紀謂纂曰：「主上闇弱，未堪多難。

translations.literal: Hong secretly sent Master of Writing Jiang Ji to tell Zuan: "The lord on high is weak and dark—not fit to bear many troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Hong secretly sent Master of Writing Jiang Ji to Zuan: "The sovereign is feeble and cannot weather these troubles.

sentences.zh: 兄威恩素著，宜為社稷計，不可徇小節也。」

translations.literal: Elder brother, your prestige and grace have long been renowned—you should plan for the altars of soil and grain; you cannot cling to small proprieties."
translations.idiomatic: Your prestige is established. Act for the realm—not for petty scruples."

sentences.zh: 纂於是夜帥壯士數百逾北城，攻廣夏門，弘帥東苑之眾斧洪範門。

translations.literal: Zuan thereupon that night led several hundred stalwarts over the north wall, attacked the Gate of Broad Summer; Hong led the forces of the Eastern Park to axe through the Gate of Grand Norm.
translations.idiomatic: That night Zuan led several hundred picked men over the north wall and stormed the Gate of Broad Summer. Hong led the Eastern Park garrison to break through the Gate of Grand Norm.

sentences.zh: 左衛將軍齊從守融明觀，逆問之曰：「誰也？」

translations.literal: Left Guard General Qi Cong guarded the Rongming Pavilion; he went against them and asked: "Who is it?"
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard General Qi Cong held the Rongming Watchtower and challenged them: "Who goes there?"

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「太原公。」

translations.literal: The crowd said: "The Prince of Taiyuan."
translations.idiomatic: The answer came: "The Prince of Taiyuan."

sentences.zh: 從曰：「國有大故，主上新立，太原公行不由道，夜入禁城，將為亂邪？」」

translations.literal: Cong said: "The state has a great mourning; the lord on high is newly established; the Prince of Taiyuan travels not by the proper path, enters the forbidden city by night—is he about to make rebellion?"
translations.idiomatic: Cong said, "The realm is in mourning and the sovereign is newly enthroned. The Prince of Taiyuan enters the palace by night by an unlawful way—is this mutiny?"

sentences.zh: 因抽劍直前斫纂，中額，纂左右禽之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drew his sword and straight ahead hacked at Zuan, hit his forehead; Zuan's attendants seized him.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his sword and struck at Zuan, wounding his forehead. Zuan's men seized him.

sentences.zh: 纂曰：「義士也，勿殺！」；

translations.literal: Zuan said: "A man of duty—do not kill him!"
translations.idiomatic: Zuan cried, "He is a loyal man. Do not kill him!"

sentences.zh: 紹遣虎賁中郎將呂開帥禁兵拒戰於端門，呂超帥卒二千赴之；

translations.literal: Shao sent Tiger Guard Palace Attendant Lü Kai leading forbidden troops to resist battle at the Duan Gate; Lü Chao led two thousand men to join them;
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent Tiger Guard Lü Kai with the palace guard to hold the Duan Gate. Lü Chao brought two thousand men to reinforce him;

sentences.zh: 眾素憚纂，皆不戰而潰。

translations.literal: the crowd had long feared Zuan; all fought not and were routed.
translations.idiomatic: but the troops had long feared Zuan. None would fight and they broke.

sentences.zh: 纂入自青角門，升謙光殿。

translations.literal: Zuan entered from the Blue Horn Gate and ascended the Qian'guang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan entered through the Blue Horn Gate and ascended the Hall of Modest Light.

sentences.zh: 紹登紫閣自殺。

translations.literal: Shao ascended the Purple Pavilion and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shao climbed the Purple Pavilion and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 呂超奔廣武。。

translations.literal: Lü Chao fled to Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chao fled to Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 纂憚弘兵強，以位讓弘。

translations.literal: Zuan feared Hong's troops were strong and yielded the throne to Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan, wary of Hong's strength, offered him the throne.

sentences.zh: 弘曰：「弘以紹弟也，而承大統，眾心不順，是以違先帝遺命而廢之，慚負黃泉！

translations.literal: Hong said: "Hong, being Shao's younger brother, yet received the great succession—the people's hearts did not accord; therefore I violated the late emperor's testamentary command and deposed him—I am ashamed before the Yellow Springs!
translations.idiomatic: Hong said, "I am Shao's younger brother, yet I took the throne against the people's will. I already defied our father's dying charge in deposing him—I am ashamed before the dead!

sentences.zh: 今復逾兄而立，豈弘之本志乎！」

translations.literal: Now again to pass over elder brother and be established—how is that Hong's original intent!"
translations.idiomatic: How could my heart consent to leap over my elder brother now!"

sentences.zh: 纂乃使弘出告眾曰：「先帝臨終，受詔如此。」

translations.literal: Zuan thereupon had Hong go out and tell the crowd: "The late emperor at his end received an edict thus."
translations.idiomatic: Zuan had Hong announce to the court: "This was our father's dying charge."

sentences.zh: 群臣皆曰：「苟社稷有主，誰敢違者！」

translations.literal: The officials all said: "If the altars of soil and grain have a lord, who dares disobey!"
translations.idiomatic: The ministers answered as one: "So long as the realm has a master, who would disobey?"

sentences.zh: 纂遂即天王位。

translations.literal: Zuan thereupon ascended the Heavenly King's throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan then took the throne as Heavenly King.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元咸寧，謚光曰懿武皇帝，廟號太祖；

translations.literal: A great amnesty; changed the era to Xianning; posthumous title for Guang was Emperor Yi and Martial; temple name Taizu;
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty, adopted the era Xianning, and posthumously titled Guang Emperor Yi and Martial with temple name Taizu;

sentences.zh: 謚紹曰隱王。

translations.literal: posthumous title for Shao was King Yin.
translations.idiomatic: and gave Shao the posthumous name King Yin.

sentences.zh: 以弘為大都督、督中外諸軍事、大司馬、車騎大將軍、司隸校尉、錄尚書事，改封番禾郡公。。

translations.literal: He made Hong Grand Commander, Director of all military affairs within and without, Grand Marshal, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Director of the Intendancy of the Capital, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and changed his enfeoffment to Duke of Fanhe Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was made Grand Commander, Director of all military affairs civil and martial, Grand Marshal, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Director of the Metropolitan Intendancy, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, with a new enfeoffment as Duke of Fanhe.

sentences.zh: 纂謂齊從曰：「卿前斫我，一何甚也！」

translations.literal: Zuan said to Qi Cong: "You before hacked me—how very severe!"
translations.idiomatic: Zuan said to Qi Cong, "Your blow was fierce indeed!"

sentences.zh: 從泣曰：「隱王，先帝所立；

translations.literal: Cong wept and said: "King Yin—the late emperor established him;
translations.idiomatic: Cong wept and said, "King Yin was chosen by our late lord;

sentences.zh: 陛下雖應天順人，而微心未達，唯恐陛下不死，何謂甚也！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty may have answered Heaven and followed the people's will, yet my inner thought has not reached you—I only feared Your Majesty would not die. What do you mean by saying I was too severe!"
translations.idiomatic: "You may have Heaven and men on your side, but you never understood my heart—I feared only that you would survive. What do you mean my blow was too fierce?"

sentences.zh: 纂賞其忠，善遇之。。

translations.literal: Zuan rewarded his loyalty and treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan praised his loyalty and treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 纂叔父征東將軍方鎮廣武，纂遣使謂方曰：「超實忠臣，義勇可嘉，但不識國家大體，權變之宜。

translations.literal: Zuan's uncle the General Who Conquers the East Fang held Guangwu. Zuan sent an envoy to tell Fang: "Chao is indeed a loyal minister—his righteous courage is admirable—but he does not understand the great principle of the state or what flexibility requires.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's uncle Fang, General Who Conquers the East and governor of Guangwu, sent Fang a message: "Chao is loyal and brave, but he lacks sense of the state's larger needs and when to bend with circumstances.

sentences.zh: 方賴其用，以濟世難，可以此意諭之。」

translations.literal: Fang relies on his use to deliver the age from its troubles—you may expound this idea to him."
translations.idiomatic: I depend on him to see us through this crisis. Explain that to him."

sentences.zh: 超上疏陳謝，纂復其爵位。。

translations.literal: Chao submitted a memorial expressing thanks; Zuan restored his rank and title.
translations.idiomatic: Chao memorialized his gratitude, and Zuan restored his titles.

sentences.zh: 是歲，燕主盛以河間公熙為都督中外諸軍事、尚書左僕射，領中領軍。。

translations.literal: That year, the Yan ruler Sheng made the Duke of Hejian Xi Director of all military affairs within and without, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and concurrent Central Commander of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: That year Murong Sheng of Yan named Duke of Hejian Xi grand commander of all armies, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and acting commander of the central guard.

sentences.zh: 劉衛辰子文陳降魏；

translations.literal: Liu Weichen's son Wenchen surrendered to Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Weichen's son Wenchen defected to Wei;

sentences.zh: 魏主珪妻以宗女，拜上將軍，賜姓宿氏。。

translations.literal: the Wei ruler Gui gave him a clanswoman in marriage, appointed him Grand General, and bestowed the surname Su.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui married him to a royal clanswoman, made him Grand General, and granted him the surname Su.

sentences.zh: 安皇帝丙隆安四年（庚子，公元四零零年） 。

translations.literal: Emperor An, year 4 of Longan (gengzi, AD 400).
translations.idiomatic: Year 4 of Longan under Emperor An of Jin (gengzi, AD 400).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬子朔，燕主盛大赦，自貶號為庶人天王。。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day renzi, the first of the month, the Yan ruler Sheng proclaimed a great amnesty and demoted his title to Commoner Heavenly King.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the new moon of the first month, Murong Sheng proclaimed an amnesty and styled himself Commoner Heavenly King.

sentences.zh: 魏材官將軍和跋襲盧溥於遼西，戊午，克之，禽溥及其子煥，送平城，車裂之。

translations.literal: Wei's Material-Officers General He Ba attacked Lu Pu in Liaoxi; on the day wuwu he captured it, seized Pu and his son Huan, sent them to Pingcheng, and executed them by dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Material-Officers General He Ba struck Lu Pu in Liaoxi. On wuwu day he took the place, captured Pu and his son Huan, sent them to Pingcheng, and tore them apart with chariots.

sentences.zh: 燕主盛遣廣威將軍孟廣平救溥，不及，斬魏遼西守宰而還。。

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Sheng sent the General of Broad Authority Meng Guangping to rescue Pu; he did not arrive in time and, having beheaded Wei's Liaoxi officials, returned.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Sheng sent General of Broad Authority Meng Guangping to relieve Pu, but arrived too late; he beheaded the Wei garrison in Liaoxi and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，大赦。。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 西秦王乾歸遷都苑川。。

translations.literal: The Western Qin king Qiangui moved the capital to Yuanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui of Western Qin moved his capital to Yuanchuan.

sentences.zh: 禿髮利鹿孤大赦，改元建和。。

translations.literal: Tufa Lilugu proclaimed a great amnesty and changed the era to Jianhe.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Lilugu of Southern Liang proclaimed an amnesty and adopted the era Jianhe.

sentences.zh: 高句麗王安事燕禮慢；

translations.literal: An, king of Goguryeo, was slow in observing courtesy toward Yan;
translations.idiomatic: King An of Goguryeo slighted Yan in the matter of tribute;

sentences.zh: 二月，丙申，燕王盛自將兵三萬襲之，以驃騎大將國熙為前鋒，拔新城、南蘇二城，開境七百餘里，徙五千餘戶而還。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day bingshen, the Yan king Sheng personally led thirty thousand troops to strike him, with General of Swift Cavalry Guo Xi as vanguard; he took the two cities Xincheng and Nansu, opened territory more than seven hundred li, moved more than five thousand households, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on bingshen day, Murong Sheng led thirty thousand men against him, with Guo Xi commanding the van. He seized Xincheng and Nansu, pushed the frontier seven hundred li, resettled five thousand households, and marched home.

sentences.zh: 熙勇冠諸將，盛曰：「叔父雄果，有世祖之風，但弘略不如耳！」。

translations.literal: Xi's courage topped all the generals. Sheng said: "Uncle, you are bold and resolute—you have the style of our founding ancestor—but your largeness of design is not his equal!"
translations.idiomatic: Xi was the bravest of the commanders. Sheng said, "Uncle, your boldness matches our founder's—only your breadth of vision falls short!"

sentences.zh: 初，魏主珪納劉頭眷之女，寵冠後庭，生子嗣。

translations.literal: At the outset, the Wei ruler Gui took in Liu Toujuan's daughter; her favor topped the inner palace, and she bore a son, Si.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Tuoba Gui had taken Liu Toujuan's daughter; she outshone every consort and bore a son named Si.

sentences.zh: 及克中山，獲燕主寶之幼女。

translations.literal: When he captured Zhongshan, he obtained the Yan ruler Bao's young daughter.
translations.idiomatic: After he took Zhongshan he also gained Murong Bao's young daughter.

sentences.zh: 將立皇后，用其國故事，鑄金人以卜之，劉氏所鑄不成，慕容氏成，三月，戊午，立慕容氏為皇后。。

translations.literal: When about to establish an empress, following his state's old custom he cast golden human figures to divine by them; the one cast by the Liu clan did not succeed, the one by the Murong clan did; in the third month, on the day wuwu, he established Lady Murong as empress.
translations.idiomatic: To choose an empress he followed Wei custom and cast golden figures as lots—the Liu figure failed, the Murong figure held. On wuwu day in the third month he made Lady Murong empress.

sentences.zh: 桓玄既克荊、雍，表求領荊、江二州。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan, having conquered Jing and Yong, memorialized requesting to hold the two provinces Jing and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Xuan seized Jing and Yong, he asked to be given both Jing and Jiang provinces.

sentences.zh: 詔以玄為都督荊、司、雍、秦、染、益、寧七州諸軍事、荊州刺史，以中護軍桓修為江州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict made Xuan Director of military affairs for the seven provinces Jing, Si, Yong, Qin, Liang, Yi, and Ning, and Inspector of Jing; the Central Guard General Huan Xiu was made Inspector of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: The court named Xuan director of armies in Jing, Si, Yong, Qin, Liang, Yi, and Ning and inspector of Jing, with Huan Xiu as inspector of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 玄上疏固求江州，於是進玄督八州及揚、豫八部諸軍事，復領江州刺史。

translations.literal: Xuan memorialized obstinately requesting Jiang province; thereupon Xuan was advanced to Director of eight provinces and military affairs of Yang and Yu's eight commanderies, and again concurrently held the post of Inspector of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan pressed his claim to Jiang until the court enlarged his mandate to eight provinces plus military command over eight Yang and Yu districts, and restored Jiang to him.

sentences.zh: 玄輒以兄偉為雍州刺史，朝廷不能違。

translations.literal: Xuan at once made his elder brother Wei Inspector of Yong—the court could not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: He promptly installed his brother Wei as inspector of Yong, and the court could not refuse.

sentences.zh: 又以從子振為淮南太守。。

translations.literal: He also made his nephew Zhen prefect of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He also named his nephew Zhen prefect of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 涼王纂以大司馬弘功高地逼，忌之。

translations.literal: The Liang king Zuan, because the Grand Marshal Hong's merit was great and his position pressing, envied him.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan of Later Liang resented Grand Marshal Hong, whose towering merit and proximity made him a threat.

sentences.zh: 弘亦自疑，遂以東苑之兵作亂，攻纂。

translations.literal: Hong also grew suspicious himself; thereupon with the troops of the Eastern Park he raised rebellion and attacked Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hong grew fearful in turn and rebelled with troops from the Eastern Park, attacking Zuan.

sentences.zh: 纂遣其將焦辨擊之，弘眾潰，出走。

translations.literal: Zuan sent his general Jiao Bian to strike him; Hong's forces collapsed and he fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan sent Jiao Bian against him; Hong's army broke and he fled.

sentences.zh: 纂縱兵大掠，悉以東苑婦女賞軍，弘之妻子亦在中。

translations.literal: Zuan let his troops plunder on a grand scale, giving all the women of the Eastern Park as rewards to the army—Hong's wife and children were among them.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan let his men loot freely and distributed the women of the Eastern Park as booty—including Hong's wife and children.

sentences.zh: 纂笑謂群臣曰：「今日之戰何如？」

translations.literal: Zuan smiled and said to the officials: "How was today's battle?"
translations.idiomatic: Zuan smiled at his court and asked, "How did today's battle go?"

sentences.zh: 侍中房晷對曰：「天禍涼室，憂患仍臻。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant Fang Gui answered: "Heaven's calamity upon the house of Liang—troubles still arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Fang Gui replied, "Heaven has cursed the house of Liang; one disaster follows another.

sentences.zh: 先帝始崩，隱王廢黜；

translations.literal: The late emperor had just died and King Yin was deposed;
translations.idiomatic: Our late lord had barely died when King Yin was cast aside;

sentences.zh: 山陵甫訖，大司馬稱兵；

translations.literal: the imperial tombs were just finished when the Grand Marshal raised arms;
translations.idiomatic: the tombs were scarcely sealed when the Grand Marshal took up arms;

sentences.zh: 京師流血，昆弟接刃。

translations.literal: the capital ran with blood and brothers crossed blades.
translations.idiomatic: blood ran in the capital and brothers turned on one another.

sentences.zh: 雖弘自取夷滅，亦由陛下無棠棣之恩，當省己責躬謝百姓。

translations.literal: Although Hong brought extinction on himself, it is also because Your Majesty lacked the affection of the humble tree-pear—You should examine Yourself, blame Yourself, and apologize to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Hong courted ruin, yet Your Majesty showed no brotherly grace. You should search your heart, accept blame, and make amends to the people.

sentences.zh: 乃更縱兵大掠，囚辱士女，釁自弘起，百姓何罪！

translations.literal: Yet You still further let troops plunder on a grand scale, imprisoning and shaming scholars and women—the provocation arose from Hong—what crime have the common people!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you went on looting and abusing men and women—Hong started this; what did the people do to deserve it?

sentences.zh: 且弘妻，陛下之弟婦，弘女，陛下之侄也，奈何使無賴小人辱為婢妾！

translations.literal: Moreover Hong's wife is Your Majesty's younger brother's wife; Hong's daughter is Your Majesty's niece—how can You let worthless ruffians shame them as maidservants and concubines!
translations.idiomatic: Hong's wife is your brother's widow; his daughter is your niece. How can you let rabble dishonor them as slaves?

sentences.zh: 天地神明，豈忍見此！」

translations.literal: Heaven and earth and the spirits—how could they bear to witness this!"
translations.idiomatic: Could Heaven itself endure to see this?"

sentences.zh: 遂歔欷流涕。

translations.literal: Then he sobbed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He broke down in tears.

sentences.zh: 纂改容謝之，召弘妻子寘於東宮，厚撫之。。

translations.literal: Zuan changed his expression and apologized to him; he summoned Hong's wife and children and placed them in the Eastern Palace, treating them generously.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's face changed; he apologized and had Hong's family housed in the Eastern Palace with rich care.

sentences.zh: 弘將奔禿髮利鹿孤，道過廣武，詣呂方。

translations.literal: Hong was about to flee to Tufa Lilugu; passing Guangwu on the way, he went to see Lü Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Hong fled toward Tufa Lilugu; passing Guangwu he sought out Lü Fang.

sentences.zh: 方見之，大哭曰：「天下甚寬，汝何為至此！」

translations.literal: When Fang saw him, he wept loudly and said: "The world is very wide—why have you come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Fang wept at the sight of him: "The world is wide—how did you end up here?"

sentences.zh: 乃執弘送獄，纂遣力士康龍就拉殺之。。

translations.literal: Thereupon he seized Hong and sent him to prison; Zuan dispatched the strongman Kang Long to go and strangle him to death.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Hong and sent him to prison; Zuan sent the brawler Kang Long to strangle him where he lay.

sentences.zh: 纂立妃楊氏為後，以後父桓為尚書左僕射、涼都尹。。

translations.literal: Zuan established his consort Lady Yang as empress and made the empress's father Huan Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Governor of the Capital of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan made Lady Yang empress and her father Huan Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and chief magistrate of the Liang capital.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，燕襄平令段登等謀反，誅。。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, Duan Deng, magistrate of Xiangping under Yan, and others plotted rebellion and were executed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day Duan Deng, magistrate of Xiangping, and others were executed for treason.

sentences.zh: 涼王纂將伐武威王利鹿孤，中書令楊穎諫曰：「利鹿孤上下用命，國未有釁，不可伐也。」

translations.literal: The Liang king Zuan was about to attack the Liang of Wuwei king Lilugu; the Director of the Masters of Writing Yang Ying remonstrated: "Lilugu has superiors and subordinates all giving their orders; the state has no breach—one must not attack."
translations.idiomatic: Zuan prepared to attack Tufa Lilugu of Wuwei. Director of the Masters of Writing Yang Ying warned, "Lilugu's realm serves him united; there is no opening—do not attack."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: He did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan refused.

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤使其弟佺檁拒之，夏，四月，辱檁敗涼兵於三堆，斬首二千餘級。。

translations.literal: Lilugu sent his younger brother Rutan to resist; in summer, the fourth month, Rutan defeated the Liang army at Sandui and took more than two thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu sent his brother Rutan to meet them. In the fourth month of summer Rutan routed the Liang army at Sandui, claiming two thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 初，隴西李暠好文學，有令名。

translations.literal: At the outset, Li Gao of Longxi loved literature and had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao of Longxi was a literary man of fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 嘗與郭□及同母弟敦煌宋繇同宿，□起謂繇曰：「君當位極人臣，李君終當有國家；

translations.literal: He once lodged overnight with Guo Nen and his uterine younger brother Song Yao of Dunhuang; Nen rose and said to Yao: "You will reach the summit of ministerial rank; Lord Li in the end will possess a state;
translations.idiomatic: Once he shared lodgings with Guo Nen and his half-brother Song Yao of Dunhuang. Nen told Yao, "You will rise to the top of the bureaucracy; Li is fated to rule a state of his own;

sentences.zh: 有騍馬生白額駒。

translations.literal: when a piebald mare bears a white-browed colt.
translations.idiomatic: when your dun mare foals a white-faced colt.

sentences.zh: 此其時也。」

translations.literal: That will be the hour."
translations.idiomatic: That will be the sign."

sentences.zh: 及孟繁為沙州刺史，以暠為效谷令；

translations.literal: When Meng Min became Inspector of Sha, he made Gao magistrate of Xiaogu;
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Min became prefect of Sha, he made Li Gao magistrate of Xiaogu;

sentences.zh: 宋繇事北涼王業，為中散常侍。

translations.literal: Song Yao served the Northern Liang king Ye as Regular Palace Attendant in the Central Dispersal.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yao served Duan Ye of Northern Liang as a Central Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 孟敏卒，敦煌護軍馮翊郭謙、沙州治中敦煌索仙等以暠溫毅有惠政，推為敦煌太守。

translations.literal: When Meng Min died, Dunhuang Protector Guo Qian of Fuping, Sha Province Administrator Suo Xian of Dunhuang, and others, because Gao was mild, resolute, and had benevolent government, recommended him as Prefect of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Min died, protector Guo Qian and administrator Suo Xian, finding Li Gao gentle, firm, and just in office, raised him to prefect of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 暠初難之，會宋繇自張掖告歸，謂暠曰：「段王無遠略，終必無成。

translations.literal: Gao at first demurred; it happened that Song Yao, on leave returning from Zhangye, said to Gao: "Prince Duan lacks far-reaching design—he will in the end accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao hesitated until Song Yao came home on leave from Zhangye and said, "Duan Ye has no long view—he cannot last.

sentences.zh: 兄忘郭暠之言邪？

translations.literal: Elder brother, have you forgotten Guo Nen's words?
translations.idiomatic: Brother, have you forgotten what Guo Nen foretold?

sentences.zh: 白額駒今已生矣。」

translations.literal: The white-browed colt has now been born."
translations.idiomatic: The white-faced colt has already arrived."

sentences.zh: 暠乃從之，遣使請命於業；

translations.literal: Gao thereupon acceded; he sent envoys to request command from Ye;
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao agreed and asked Duan Ye to confirm the appointment.

sentences.zh: 業因以暠為敦煌太守。

translations.literal: Ye thereupon made Gao Prefect of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Ye confirmed him as prefect of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 右衛將軍敦煌索嗣言一業曰：「李暠不可使處敦煌。」

translations.literal: Right Guard General Suo Si of Dunhuang said to Ye: "Li Gao must not be allowed to hold Dunhuang."
translations.idiomatic: Right Guard General Suo Si of Dunhuang told Ye, "Li Gao should not be left in Dunhuang."

sentences.zh: 業以嗣代日++高為敦煌太守，使帥五百騎之官。

translations.literal: Ye replaced Gao with Si as Prefect of Dunhuang and sent him to take office at the head of five hundred horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Ye replaced Li Gao with Si as prefect and sent him west with five hundred cavalry.

sentences.zh: 嗣未至二十里，移暠犯己；

translations.literal: Before Si had reached twenty li, he sent orders that Gao was offending against him;
translations.idiomatic: Twenty li short of the city Si announced that Gao was moving against him;

sentences.zh: 暠驚疑，將出迎之。

translations.literal: Gao was alarmed and suspicious and was about to go out to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao, startled, prepared to ride out to receive him.

sentences.zh: 效谷令張邈及宋繇止之曰：「段王闇弱，正是英豪有為之日；

translations.literal: Xiaogu Magistrate Zhang Miao and Song Yao stopped him and said: "Prince Duan is dim and weak—this is exactly the day for a hero to act;
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Zhang Miao and Song Yao stopped him: "Duan Ye is weak and blind—this is the hour for a man of action;

sentences.zh: 將軍據一國成資，奈何拱手授人！

translations.literal: General, you hold a state's complete resources—why hand them over with folded arms!
translations.idiomatic: You hold a whole province in your hands—why surrender it without a fight?

sentences.zh: 嗣自恃本郡，謂人情附己，不意將軍猝能拒之，可一戰擒也。」

translations.literal: Si, relying on being from this commandery, thought the people's hearts attached to him and did not expect the General suddenly could resist him—he can be captured in one battle."
translations.idiomatic: Si trusts his native ties and thinks the people favor him; he will never expect you to resist—one battle will take him."

sentences.zh: 暠從之。

translations.literal: Gao followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao agreed.

sentences.zh: 無遣繇見嗣，啖以甘言。

translations.literal: First he sent Yao to see Si and fed him with sweet words.
translations.idiomatic: He first sent Song Yao to meet Si with fair promises.

sentences.zh: 繇還，謂暠曰：「嗣志驕兵弱，易取也。」

translations.literal: Yao returned and said to Gao: "Si's will is arrogant and his troops weak—he is easy to take."
translations.idiomatic: Yao returned and reported, "Si is overconfident and his force is slight—he can be taken easily."

sentences.zh: 暠乃遣邈、繇與其二子歆、讓逆擊之，嗣敗走，還張掖。

translations.literal: Gao thereupon sent Miao, Yao, and his two sons Xin and Rang to strike him in opposition; Si was defeated and fled, returning to Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao sent Zhang Miao, Song Yao, and his sons Xin and Rang to attack. Si was routed and fled back to Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 暠素與嗣善，尤恨之，表業請誅嗣。

translations.literal: Gao had always been on good terms with Si and hated him all the more; he memorialized Ye requesting Si's execution.
translations.idiomatic: Though they had once been friends, Li Gao now hated Si deeply and asked Ye to execute him.

sentences.zh: 沮渠男成亦惡嗣，勸業除之；

translations.literal: Juqu Mancheng also hated Si and urged Ye to remove him;
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mancheng likewise despised Si and urged Ye to kill him;

sentences.zh: 業乃殺嗣，遣使謝暠，進暠都督涼興已西諸軍事、鎮西將軍。。

translations.literal: Ye thereupon killed Si, sent envoys to apologize to Gao, and advanced Gao to Director of military affairs west of Liang and Xing and General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: Ye executed Si, apologized to Li Gao, and promoted him to director of armies west of Liang and Xing and General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾視羆卒，世子樹洛干方九歲，弟烏紇堤立。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun Shipi died; the heir Tuyuhun Shiluogan was just nine years old, and his younger brother Wugeti was established.
translations.idiomatic: Shipi of the Tuyuhun died. His heir Shiluogan was only nine; his younger brother Wugeti was enthroned.

sentences.zh: 妻樹洛干之母念氏，生慕瑰、慕延。

translations.literal: He took as wife Shiluogan's mother Lady Nian, who bore Mugui and Muyan.
translations.idiomatic: Wugeti married Shiluogan's mother, Lady Nian, who bore Mugui and Muyan.

sentences.zh: 烏紇堤懦弱荒淫，不能治國；

translations.literal: Wugeti was weak, debauched, and unable to govern the state;
translations.idiomatic: Wugeti was feckless and dissolute and could not govern;

sentences.zh: 念氏專制國事，有膽智，國人畏服之。。

translations.literal: Lady Nian monopolized state affairs; she had courage and wisdom, and the people of the state feared and submitted to her.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Nian ran the realm with courage and wit, and her people obeyed her in awe.

sentences.zh: 燕前將軍段璣，太后段氏之兄子也，為段登辭所連及，五月，壬子，逃奔遼西。。

translations.literal: Duan Ji, Former General of Yan and nephew of Empress Dowager Duan's elder brother, was implicated through Duan Deng's confession; in the fifth month, on the day renzi, he fled to Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ji, Former General of Yan and a nephew of Empress Dowager Duan, was named in Duan Deng's confession. On renzi day in the fifth month he fled to Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，衛將軍東亭獻侯王珣卒。。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, the General of the Guard, Marquis Xian of Dongting, Wang Xun, died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day, General of the Guard Wang Xun, Marquis Xian of Dongting, died.

sentences.zh: 己巳，魏主珪東如涿鹿，西如馬邑，觀□源。。

translations.literal: On the day jisi, the Wei ruler Gui went east to Zhuolu and west to Mayi to view the source of the Lei River.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day, the Wei ruler Tuoba Gui traveled east to Zhuolu and west to Mayi to inspect the source of the Lei River.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，燕段璣復還歸罪；

translations.literal: On the day wuyin, Duan Ji of Yan returned once more to submit to judgment;
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day, Duan Ji of Yan came back to Yan to surrender himself;

sentences.zh: 燕王盛赦之，賜號曰思悔侯，使尚公主，入直殿內。。

translations.literal: The Yan king Sheng pardoned him, bestowed the title Marquis Reflecting on Repentance, had him marry a princess, and admitted him to palace duty within the halls.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Sheng pardoned him, created him Marquis Reflecting on Repentance, married him to a princess, and posted him on duty inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 謝琰以資望鎮會稽，不能綏懷，又不為武備。

translations.literal: Xie Yan, by virtue of his standing, guarded Kuaiji, yet could neither soothe and embrace the people nor make military preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yan held Kuaiji on the strength of his family name, but he neither won the people over nor kept the garrison ready.

sentences.zh: 諸將鹹諫曰：「賊近在海浦，伺人形便，宜開其自新之路。」

translations.literal: The generals all remonstrated, saying: "The rebels are near on the seacoast, watching for an opportune moment in men's affairs; we should open a path for them to reform themselves."
translations.idiomatic: His generals all urged him: "The rebels are camped on the coast, waiting for an opening. We ought to offer them a way back to loyalty."

sentences.zh: 琰不從，曰：「苻堅之眾百萬，尚送死淮南；

translations.literal: Yan would not listen and said: "Fu Jian's host of a million men still went to meet death at Huainan;
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yan refused. "Even Fu Jian's million-man army marched to its death at Huainan;

sentences.zh: 孫恩小賊，敗死入海，何能復出！

translations.literal: Sun En is a petty bandit who fled defeated into the sea—how could he emerge again!
translations.idiomatic: Sun En is a petty rebel who fled beaten into the sea. How could he ever come back!

sentences.zh: 若其果出，是天欲殺之也。」

translations.literal: If he truly comes out again, it will mean Heaven itself wishes to destroy him."
translations.idiomatic: If he does return, Heaven itself must want him dead."

sentences.zh: 既而恩寇浹口，入餘姚，破上虞。

translations.literal: Before long Sun En raided Jiakou, entered Yuyao, and took Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Sun En struck Jiakou, entered Yuyao, and overran Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 進及邢浦，琰遣參軍劉宣之擊破之，恩退走。

translations.literal: Advancing as far as Xingpu, Yan sent his aide Liu Xuanzhi to attack and defeat him, and En withdrew in flight.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun En reached Xingpu, Xie Yan sent his aide Liu Xuanzhi against him and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 少日，復寇邢浦，官軍失利，恩乘勝徑進。

translations.literal: Within a few days he raided Xingpu again; the government army was defeated, and En pressed his advantage straight onward.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he struck Xingpu again. The imperial forces lost, and Sun En pressed straight on.

sentences.zh: 己卯，至會稽。

translations.literal: On the day jimao, he reached Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day he reached Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 琰尚未食，曰：「要當先滅此賊而後食。」

translations.literal: Yan had not yet eaten and said: "I must first destroy these bandits and only then eat."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yan had not yet eaten and said, "I mean to destroy these rebels before I sit down to a meal."

sentences.zh: 因跨馬出戰，兵敗，為帳下都督張猛所殺。

translations.literal: Thereupon he mounted his horse and went out to battle; his army was defeated, and he was killed by Zhang Meng, commander of his personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: He mounted and rode out to fight, was routed, and was killed by Zhang Meng, a commander of his household guard.

sentences.zh: 吳興太守庾桓恐郡民復應恩，殺男女數千人。

translations.literal: Yu Huan, Prefect of Wuxing, fearing that the people of the commandery would again respond to En, killed several thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Huan, prefect of Wuxing, fearing the county would rally to Sun En again, slaughtered several thousand men and women.

sentences.zh: 恩轉寇臨海。

translations.literal: En turned to raid Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En then turned against Linhai.

sentences.zh: 朝廷大震，遣冠軍將軍桓不才、輔國將軍孫無終、寧朔將軍高雅之拒之。。

translations.literal: The court was greatly shaken and dispatched the Champion General Huan Bucai, the General Who Supports the State Sun Wuzhong, and the General Who Pacifies the North Gao Yazhi to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: The court was alarmed and sent Champion General Huan Bucai, General Who Supports the State Sun Wuzhong, and General Who Pacifies the North Gao Yazhi to meet him.

sentences.zh: 秦征西大將軍隴西公碩德將兵五千伐西秦，入自南安峽。

translations.literal: Qin's Grand General Who Conquers the West, the Duke of Longxi Shuode, led five thousand troops to attack Western Qin, entering by way of the Nan'an Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: Shuode, Duke of Longxi and Qin Grand General Who Conquers the West, marched five thousand men against Western Qin through the Nan'an Gorge.

sentences.zh: 西秦王乾歸帥諸將拒之，軍於隴西。。

translations.literal: Qifu Gangui, king of Western Qin, led his generals to resist, encamping in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui of Western Qin led his generals out to meet them and camped in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 楊軌、田玄明謀殺武威王利鹿孤，利鹿孤殺之。。

translations.literal: Yang Gui and Tian Xuanming plotted to kill Lilugu, Prince of Wuwei; Lilugu killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gui and Tian Xuanming plotted to kill Lilugu, Prince of Wuwei, and Lilugu had them executed.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚辰朔，日有食之。。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the first day gengchen, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the first day gengchen, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 以琅邪王師何澄為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He Cheng, Preceptor to the Prince of Langye, was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He Cheng, preceptor to the Prince of Langye, was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 澄，准之子也。。

translations.literal: Cheng was the son of He Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: He Cheng was a son of He Zhun.

sentences.zh: 甲子，燕大赦。。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, Yan proclaimed a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day, Yan proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 涼王纂將襲北涼，姜紀諫曰：「盛夏農事方殷，且宜息兵。

translations.literal: The Liang king Zuan was about to attack Northern Liang. Jiang Ji remonstrated, saying: "In the height of summer farming is at its busiest; for the moment we ought to rest the army.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan, king of Later Liang, was preparing to strike Northern Liang. Jiang Ji warned him: "It is midsummer and the fields are at their busiest. This is no time for war.

sentences.zh: 今遠出嶺西，禿髮氏乘虛襲京師，將若之何！」

translations.literal: Now, marching far west of the mountains, if the Tufa clan seizes the opening to strike the capital, what then are we to do!"
translations.idiomatic: If you march deep into the country west of the passes, the Tufa will strike our capital while it stands empty. What then!"

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: He did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan refused.

sentences.zh: 進圍張掖，西掠建康。

translations.literal: He advanced to besiege Zhangye and raided west into Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to besiege Zhangye and swept west through Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 禿髮辱檁聞之，將萬騎襲姑臧，纂弟隴西公緯賃北城以自固。

translations.literal: When Tufa Rutan heard of it, he led ten thousand horsemen to strike Guzang; Zuan's younger brother, the Duke of Longxi Wei, encamped in the northern city to hold fast.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Rutan heard of it and led ten thousand cavalry against Guzang. Zuan's brother Wei, Duke of Longxi, fortified the northern city to hold out.

sentences.zh: 辱檀置酒朱明門上，鳴鐘鼓，饗將士，曜兵於青陽門，掠八千餘戶而去。

translations.literal: Rutan set out wine atop the Zhu Ming Gate, sounded bells and drums, feasted his officers and soldiers, displayed his troops at the Qingyang Gate, and carried off more than eight thousand households before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan feasted his troops atop the Zhu Ming Gate with bells and drums, paraded his army at the Qingyang Gate, and withdrew after seizing more than eight thousand households.

sentences.zh: 纂聞之，引兵還。。

translations.literal: When Zuan heard of it, he led his army back.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuan heard, he turned his army homeward.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬子，太皇太后李氏崩。。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day renzi, Grand Empress Dowager Li died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on renzi day, Grand Empress Dowager Li died.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，大赦。。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, there was a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 西秦王乾歸使武衛將軍慕兀等屯守，秦軍樵采路絕，秦王興潛引兵救之。

translations.literal: Qifu Gangui, king of Western Qin, sent the Martial Guard General Mu Wu and others to hold positions in garrison; the Qin army's routes for gathering firewood were cut off, and the Qin king Xing secretly led troops to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui posted Martial Guard General Mu Wu and others to hold the line, cutting off the Qin army's firewood routes. Yao Xing of Qin secretly marched to their relief.

sentences.zh: 乾歸聞之，使慕兀帥中軍二萬屯柏楊，鎮軍將軍羅敦帥外軍四萬屯侯辰谷，乾歸自將輕騎數千前候秦兵。

translations.literal: When Gangui heard of it, he had Mu Wu lead twenty thousand men of the central army to encamp at Baiyang; the Pacifying Army General Luo Dun lead forty thousand men of the outer army to encamp at Houchen Valley; and Gangui himself led several thousand light horsemen forward to reconnoiter the Qin army.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui sent Mu Wu with twenty thousand central troops to Baiyang and Pacifying Army General Luo Dun with forty thousand outer troops to Houchen Valley, while he himself rode ahead with several thousand light cavalry to watch the Qin advance.

sentences.zh: 會大風昏霧，與中軍相失，為追騎所逼，入於外軍。

translations.literal: A great wind arose with dimming mist, and he lost contact with the central army; pressed by pursuing horsemen, he entered the outer army's lines.
translations.idiomatic: A gale and blinding mist separated him from the central army. Pursuers pressed him until he fell in among the outer troops.

sentences.zh: 旦，與秦戰，大敗，走歸苑川，其部眾三萬六千皆降於秦。

translations.literal: At dawn he fought Qin and was utterly defeated; he fled back to Yuanchuan, and his following of thirty-six thousand all surrendered to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he fought Qin and was routed. He fled to Yuanchuan, and thirty-six thousand of his followers surrendered to Qin.

sentences.zh: 興進軍枹罕。。

translations.literal: Xing advanced his army to Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing pressed on to Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 乾歸奔金城，謂諸豪帥曰；

translations.literal: Gangui fled to Jincheng and said to the various powerful chieftains:
translations.idiomatic: Gangui fled to Jincheng and told the tribal chiefs:

sentences.zh: 「吾不才，叨竊名號，已逾一紀，今敗散如此，無以待敵，欲西保允吾。

translations.literal: " I am without talent, yet I have presumptuously held a royal title for more than twelve years. Now, defeated and scattered like this, I have no means to face the enemy and wish to withdraw west to hold Yunwu.
translations.idiomatic: " I have no merit, yet I have clung to a royal title for more than twelve years. Beaten and scattered as we are, I cannot face the enemy. I mean to withdraw west and hold Yunwu.

sentences.zh: 若舉國而去，必不得免；

translations.literal: If the whole state moves away together, we surely cannot escape;
translations.idiomatic: If the whole realm moves with me, none of us will escape;

sentences.zh: 卿等留此，各以其眾降秦。

translations.literal: you should remain here and each surrender to Qin with your own followers.
translations.idiomatic: stay here and each of you surrender to Qin with your own men.

sentences.zh: 以全宗族，勿吾隨也。」

translations.literal: Thus preserve your clans—do not follow me."
translations.idiomatic: Save your clans. Do not follow me."

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「死生願從陛下。」

translations.literal: They all said: "In life or death we wish to follow Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "In life or death we will follow you."

sentences.zh: 乾歸曰：「吾今將寄食於人，若天未亡我，庶幾異日克復舊業，復與卿等相見。

translations.literal: Gangui said: "I am now about to live at another's table. If Heaven has not yet destroyed me, perhaps one day I may recover my former enterprise and meet you again.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui said, "I am about to live at another man's mercy. If Heaven has not finished with me, perhaps one day I may recover my realm and see you again.

sentences.zh: 今相隨而死，無益也。」

translations.literal: To follow me now and die together would be of no use."
translations.idiomatic: To follow me now and die together would serve no purpose."

sentences.zh: 乃大哭而別。

translations.literal: Thereupon they wept greatly and parted.
translations.idiomatic: Then they wept and took leave of one another.

sentences.zh: 乾歸獨引數百騎奔允吾，乞降於武威王利鹿孤，利鹿孤遣廣武公辱檀迎之。

translations.literal: Gangui alone led several hundred horsemen in flight to Yunwu and begged to submit to Lilugu, Prince of Wuwei; Lilugu sent the Duke of Guangwu, Rutan, to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui rode alone with several hundred followers to Yunwu and submitted to Lilugu, Prince of Wuwei. Lilugu sent Rutan, Duke of Guangwu, to receive him.

sentences.zh: 置於晉興，待以上賓之禮。

translations.literal: He was settled at Jinxing and treated with the rites due a chief guest.
translations.idiomatic: He was lodged at Jinxing and entertained as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 鎮北將軍禿髮俱延言於利鹿孤曰：「乾歸本吾之屬國，因亂自尊，今勢窮歸命，非其誠款，若逃歸姚氏，必為國患，不如徙置乙弗之間，使不得去。」

translations.literal: The Pacifier of the North, Tufa Juyan, said to Lilugu: "Gangui was originally our dependent state. Taking advantage of disorder he raised himself up; now, with his power exhausted, he comes to submit—but this is not sincere good faith. If he escapes back to the Yao clan, he will surely become a peril to our state. Better to move him and settle him among the Yifu so that he cannot leave."
translations.idiomatic: Pacifier of the North Tufa Juyan told Lilugu, "Gangui was once our vassal. He seized a crown in the chaos, and now, broken, he comes to surrender—but his heart is false. If he slips back to the Yao, he will become a threat. Better to resettle him among the Yifu so he cannot flee."

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤曰：「彼窮來歸我，而逆疑其心，何以勸來者！」

translations.literal: Lilugu said: "He comes to us in extremity, and you would meet him with suspicion—how then are we to encourage those who come afterward!"
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu replied, "He comes to us in desperation, and you would greet him with suspicion. How will that encourage others to come!

sentences.zh: 俱延，利鹿孤之弟也。。

translations.literal: Juyan was Lilugu's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Juyan was Lilugu's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 秦兵既退，南羌梁戈等密招乾歸，乾歸將應之。

translations.literal: Once the Qin army had withdrawn, Liang Ge of the Southern Qiang and others secretly summoned Gangui, and Gangui was about to respond.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qin army withdrew, Liang Ge of the Southern Qiang and others secretly called Gangui to revolt, and he was ready to answer them.

sentences.zh: 其臣屋引阿洛以告晉興太守陰暢，暢馳白利鹿孤，利鹿孤遣其弟吐雷帥騎三千屯捫天嶺。

translations.literal: His minister Wuyin Aluo reported it to Yin Chang, Prefect of Jinxing; Chang rode at speed to inform Lilugu, and Lilugu sent his younger brother Tu Lei to lead three thousand horsemen to encamp at Mentian Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: His minister Wuyin Aluo told Jinxing Prefect Yin Chang, who rode at once to Lilugu. Lilugu sent his brother Tu Lei with three thousand cavalry to Mentian Ridge.

sentences.zh: 乾歸懼為利鹿孤所殺，謂其太子熾盤曰：「吾父子居此，必不為利鹿孤所容。

translations.literal: Gangui, fearing that Lilugu would kill him, said to his heir Chizen: "If we father and son remain here, Lilugu will surely not tolerate us.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Lilugu would kill him, Gangui told his heir Chizen, "If we stay here, Lilugu will never tolerate us.

sentences.zh: 今姚氏方強，吾將歸之，若盡室俱行，必為追騎所及，吾以汝兄弟及汝母為質，彼必不疑，吾在長安，彼終不敢害汝也。」

translations.literal: Now the Yao clan is strong, and I mean to go over to them. If the whole household travels together, we will surely be overtaken by pursuing horsemen. I shall leave you brothers and your mother as hostages; they will surely not suspect us, and once I am in Chang'an they will never dare harm you."
translations.idiomatic: The Yao are strong now, and I mean to go to them. If we all flee together, pursuers will overtake us. I will leave you, your brothers, and your mother as hostages so they will not doubt me. Once I reach Chang'an, they will never dare harm you."

sentences.zh: 乃送熾盤等於西平。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Chizen and the others to Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Chizen and the others to Xiping.

sentences.zh: 八月，乾歸南奔枹罕，遂降於秦。。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Gangui fled south to Fuhan and thereupon submitted to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Gangui fled south to Fuhan and surrendered to Qin.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，尚書左僕射王雅卒。。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, Wang Ya, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, died.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day, Wang Ya, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, died.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸丑，地震。。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day guichou, there was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guichou day, there was an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 涼呂方降於秦，廣武民三千餘戶奔武威王利鹿孤。。

translations.literal: Lü Fang of Liang submitted to Qin, and more than three thousand households of the people of Guangwu fled to Lilugu, Prince of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Fang of Later Liang surrendered to Qin, and more than three thousand households from Guangwu fled to Lilugu, Prince of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，高雅之與孫恩戰於餘姚，雅之敗，走山陰，死者什七、八。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, Gao Yazhi fought Sun En at Yuyao; Yazhi was defeated and fled to Shanyin, and seven or eight tenths of his men died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, Gao Yazhi fought Sun En at Yuyao, was beaten, and fled to Shanyin. Seven or eight men in ten were killed.

sentences.zh: 詔以劉牢之都督會稽等五郡，帥眾擊恩，恩走入海。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Liu Laozhi to command the five commanderies including Kuaiji, to lead the forces in striking En; En fled into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Liu Laozhi to command five commanderies, including Kuaiji, and drive Sun En back. Sun En fled to sea.

sentences.zh: 牢之東屯上虞，使劉裕戍句章。

translations.literal: Laozhi encamped east at Shangyu and sent Liu Yu to garrison Gouzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi camped east at Shangyu and posted Liu Yu at Gouzhang.

sentences.zh: 吳國內史袁崧築滬瀆壘以備恩。

translations.literal: Yuan Song, Interior Minister of Wu, built fortifications at the Hudu to guard against En.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Song, interior minister of Wu, built fortifications on the Hudu River to block Sun En.

sentences.zh: 崧，喬之孫也。。

translations.literal: Song was the grandson of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Song was a grandson of Yuan Qiao.

sentences.zh: 會稽世子無顯求領徐州，詔以元顯為開府儀同三司、都督揚、豫、徐、兗、青、幽、冀、並、荊、江、司、雍、梁、益、交、廣十六州諸軍事、領徐州刺史，封其子彥瑋為東海王。。

translations.literal: The heir of Kuaiji, Wuxian, requested to take charge of Xuzhou; an edict made Yuan Xian Commissioner with the Same Ceremonies as the Three Excellencies Who Open a Prefecture, Commander of Military Affairs for the sixteen provinces Yang, Yu, Xu, Yan, Qing, You, Ji, Bing, Jing, Jiang, Si, Yong, Liang, Yi, Jiao, and Guang, and Concurrent Inspector of Xuzhou, and enfeoffed his son Yanwei as Prince of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wuxian, heir of Kuaiji, asked to take Xuzhou. The court made Huan Yuanxian Commissioner with the Same Ceremonies as the Three Excellencies Who Open a Prefecture, commander of military affairs across sixteen provinces, and concurrent inspector of Xuzhou, and created his son Yanwei Prince of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 乞伏乾歸至長安，秦王興以為都督河南諸軍事、河州刺史、歸義侯。。

translations.literal: When Qifu Gangui reached Chang'an, the Qin king Xing made him Commander of Military Affairs for all south of the Yellow River, Inspector of Hezhou, and Marquis Who Returns to Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When Qifu Gangui reached Chang'an, Yao Xing made him commander of military affairs south of the Yellow River, inspector of Hezhou, and Marquis Who Returns to Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 久之，乞仗熾盤欲逃詣乾歸，武威王利鹿孤追獲之。

translations.literal: After some time, Chizen begged for weapons, intending to flee to Gangui; Lilugu, Prince of Wuwei, pursued and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: After a time Chizen begged for arms, planning to flee to Gangui. Lilugu, Prince of Wuwei, pursued and captured him.

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤將殺熾盤，廣武公辱檀曰：「子而歸父，無足深責，宜宥之以求大度。」

translations.literal: Lilugu was about to kill Chizen. The Duke of Guangwu, Rutan, said: "A son who goes back to his father is not deeply to be blamed; he should be pardoned to show magnanimity."
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu was about to execute Chizen. Rutan, Duke of Guangwu, said, "A son who seeks his father is hardly a grave crime. Pardon him and show your breadth."

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤從之。。

translations.literal: Lilugu followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu agreed.

sentences.zh: 秦王興遣晉將劉嵩等二百餘人來歸。。

translations.literal: The Qin king Xing sent more than two hundred Jin generals, including Liu Song, to come over to his side.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent more than two hundred Jin officers, including Liu Song, to defect to Qin.

sentences.zh: 北涼晉昌太守唐瑤叛，移檄六郡，推李暠為冠軍大將軍、沙州刺史、涼公、領敦煌太守。

translations.literal: Tang Yao, Prefect of Jinchang in Northern Liang, rebelled, issued a proclamation to the six commanderies, and raised Li Gao as Grand General Who Conquers the Champions, Inspector of Shazhou, Duke of Liang, and Concurrent Prefect of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yao, prefect of Jinchang in Northern Liang, rebelled, circulated a manifesto through six commanderies, and set up Li Gao as Grand General Who Conquers the Champions, inspector of Shazhou, Duke of Liang, and concurrent prefect of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 暠赦其境內，改元庚子。

translations.literal: Gao proclaimed an amnesty within his territory and changed the era name to Gengzi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao proclaimed an amnesty in his domain and adopted the era name Gengzi.

sentences.zh: 以瑤為征東將軍，郭謙為軍諮祭酒，索仙為左長史，張邈為右長史，尹建興為左司馬，張體順為右司馬。

translations.literal: He made Yao General Who Conquers the East, Guo Qian Army Consultation Libationer, Suo Xian Left Chief Clerk, Zhang Miao Right Chief Clerk, Yin Jianxing Left Major, and Zhang Tishun Right Major.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Tang Yao General Who Conquers the East, Guo Qian army consultation libationer, Suo Xian left chief clerk, Zhang Miao right chief clerk, Yin Jianxing left major, and Zhang Tishun right major.

sentences.zh: 遣從事中郎宋繇東伐涼興，並擊玉門已西諸城，皆下之。。

translations.literal: He dispatched the Attendant Gentleman Song Yao to attack Liangxing in the east, and together they struck the cities west of Yumen; all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Attendant Gentleman Song Yao east against Liangxing and together they reduced every city west of Yumen.

sentences.zh: 酒泉太守王德亦叛北涼，自稱河州刺史。

translations.literal: Wang De, Administrator of Jiuquan, also rebelled against Northern Liang and styled himself Inspector of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang De, prefect of Jiuquan, also rebelled against Northern Liang and proclaimed himself Inspector of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 北涼王業使沮渠蒙遜討之。

translations.literal: Duan Ye, king of Northern Liang, sent Juqu Mengxun to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye, king of Northern Liang, sent Juqu Mengxun to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 德焚城，將中曲奔唐瑤，蒙遜追至沙頭，大破之，虜其妻子、部落而還。。

translations.literal: De burned the city and led his central detachment in flight to Tang Yao. Mengxun pursued as far as Shatou, routed him utterly, seized his wife, children, and tribesmen, and returned.
