translations.idiomatic: De torched the city and fled with his main force toward Tang Yao. Mengxun pursued to Shatou, crushed him, and carried off his family and followers.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊寅，有星孛於天津。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day wuyin, a broom star appeared at Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuyin day, a comet appeared at the Tianjin asterism.

sentences.zh: 會稽世子元顯以星變解錄尚書事，復加尚書令。

translations.literal: Sima Yuanxian, heir of Kuaiji, citing the celestial omen resigned as Recorder of the Masters of Writing and was instead appointed Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Citing the omen in the heavens, Kuaiji heir Sima Yuanxian stepped down as Recorder of the Masters of Writing and was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing instead.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書車胤以元顯驕恣，白會稽王道子，請禁抑之。

translations.literal: Che Yin, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, because Yuanxian was arrogant and willful, informed Sima Daozi, Prince of Kuaiji, and asked that he be restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Che Yin, Minister of Personnel, reported Yuanxian's arrogance to Prince of Kuaiji Sima Daozi and asked that he be curbed.

sentences.zh: 元顯聞而未察，以問道子曰：「車武子屏人言及何事？」

translations.literal: Yuanxian heard of it but did not understand. He asked Daozi: "What did Che Wuzi discuss when he drew you aside from others?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian heard something was amiss but could not tell what. He asked Daozi, "What did Che Wuzi want to say to you in private?

sentences.zh: 道子弗答。

translations.literal: Daozi would not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi would not answer.

sentences.zh: 固問之，道子怒曰：「爾欲幽我，不令我與朝士語耶！」

translations.literal: When he pressed the question, Daozi said angrily: "Do you mean to shut me away and keep me from speaking with court officials!"
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanxian pressed him, Daozi burst out, "Are you trying to shut me up and keep me from talking to the gentlemen at court!

sentences.zh: 元顯出，謂其徒曰；

translations.literal: Yuanxian went out and said to his followers:
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian left and told his followers,

sentences.zh: 「車胤間我父子。」

translations.literal: "Che Yin is driving a wedge between my father and me."
translations.idiomatic: "Che Yin is setting my father and me against each other.

sentences.zh: 密遣人責之。

translations.literal: He secretly sent men to rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent men to rebuke Yin.

sentences.zh: 胤懼，自殺。。

translations.literal: Yin was afraid and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, in fear, took his own life.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，燕主盛立燕台，統諸部雜夷。。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, the Yan ruler Sheng established the Yan Terrace to command the various tribal peoples.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day, Murong Sheng of Yan established the Yan Terrace to oversee the various tribal peoples.

sentences.zh: 魏太史屢奏天文乖亂。

translations.literal: The Grand Astrologer of Wei repeatedly reported that the heavens were out of order.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Grand Astrologer repeatedly reported irregularities in the heavens.

sentences.zh: 魏主珪自覽占書，多雲改王易政，乃下詔風勵群下，以帝王繼統，皆有天命，不可妄干。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler Gui himself perused prognostic texts, which often spoke of changing kings and altering government. He thereupon issued an edict exhorting his subordinates that succession to the imperial throne rests on Heaven's mandate and must not be rashly attempted.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui himself read prognostic texts that often spoke of dynastic change. He issued an edict urging his officials that imperial succession rests on Heaven's mandate and must not be rashly attempted.

sentences.zh: 又數變易官名，欲以厭塞災異。

translations.literal: He also changed official titles repeatedly, hoping thereby to ward off calamities and anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: He also changed official titles again and again, hoping to ward off ill omens.

sentences.zh: 儀曹郎董謐獻《服餌仙經》，珪置仙人博士，立仙坊，煮煉百藥，封西山以供薪蒸。

translations.literal: Dong Mi, Gentleman of the Bureau of Ceremonies, presented the Scripture of Immortality through Diet and Drugs. Gui appointed an Erudite of Immortals, established an Immortals' Quarter, boiled and refined a hundred medicines, and closed off the Western Hills to supply fuel.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Mi of the Ceremonies Bureau presented the Scripture of Immortality through Diet and Drugs. Gui appointed an Erudite of Immortals, set up an Immortals' Quarter, refined elixirs from a hundred herbs, and closed the Western Hills for firewood.

sentences.zh: 藥成，令死罪者試服之，多死，不驗；

translations.literal: When the medicine was ready, he had men sentenced to death try it; many died, and it proved ineffective;
translations.idiomatic: When the elixirs were ready, he had condemned men test them. Many died, and the drugs proved worthless;

sentences.zh: 而珪猶信之，訪求不已。。

translations.literal: yet Gui still believed in it and never ceased his search.
translations.idiomatic: yet Gui still believed and never ceased his search.

sentences.zh: 珪常以燕主垂諸子分據勢要，使權柄下移，遂至敗亡，深非之。

translations.literal: Gui often held that when the Yan ruler Chui's sons each held key posts, power slipped downward and ruin followed, and he deeply disapproved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Gui often blamed Murong Chui's practice of placing his sons in powerful posts—power had slipped downward and the state had fallen—and he deeply disapproved of it.

sentences.zh: 博士公孫表希旨，上《韓非》書，勸珪以法制御下。

translations.literal: The Erudite Gongsun Biao, seeking to please him, presented the book of Han Fei and urged Gui to control his subordinates through law and regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Gongsun Biao, seeking to please him, presented Han Fei's works and urged Gui to govern his subordinates through law.

sentences.zh: 左將軍李粟性簡慢，常對珪舒放不肅，咳唾任情；

translations.literal: Li Su, Left General, was by nature blunt and disrespectful; he often behaved with easy familiarity before Gui, coughing and spitting as he pleased;
translations.idiomatic: Left General Li Su was blunt and disrespectful, often behaving with easy familiarity before Gui, coughing and spitting as he pleased;

sentences.zh: 珪積其宿過，遂誅之，群下震慄。。

translations.literal: Gui accumulated his long-standing offenses and had him executed, and all below were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Gui tallied his long record of offenses and had him executed. The court was shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，燕王盛尊獻莊後丁氏為皇太后，立遼西公定為皇太子。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, the Yan king Sheng honored Lady Ding, consort of the late Zhuang, as Empress Dowager and established the Duke of Liaoxi Ding as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day, Murong Sheng of Yan honored Lady Ding, consort of the late Zhuang, as Empress Dowager and named Duke of Liaoxi Ding crown prince.

sentences.zh: 大赦。。

translations.literal: There was a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，南燕王德即皇帝位於廣固，大赦，改元建平。

translations.literal: In this year Murong De, king of Southern Yan, assumed the imperial throne at Guanggu, proclaimed a great amnesty, and changed the reign title to Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: That year Murong De of Southern Yan took the imperial throne at Guanggu, granted a general amnesty, and proclaimed the reign title Jianping.

sentences.zh: 更名備德，欲使吏民易避。

translations.literal: He changed his name to Beide, wishing to make it easier for officials and people to avoid the taboo.
translations.idiomatic: He changed his name to Beide so that officials and commoners could more easily avoid the taboo on his personal name.

sentences.zh: 追謚燕主□曰幽皇帝。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored the Yan ruler [Chui] with the title Emperor You.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored the Yan ruler Murong Chui as Emperor You.

sentences.zh: 以北地王鐘為司徒，慕輿拔為司空，封孚為左僕射，慕輿護為右僕射。

translations.literal: He appointed Murong Zhong, Prince of Northern Yan, Grand Minister over the Masses; Murong Ba, Minister of Works; Feng Fu, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; and Murong Hu, Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He made Prince Northern Yan Zhong Grand Minister over the Masses, Murong Ba Minister of Works, Feng Fu Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Murong Hu Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 立妃段氏為皇后。。」」

translations.literal: He established Lady Duan, his consort, as empress.”
translations.idiomatic: He made his consort, Lady Duan, empress.”
